title: V999--Equipment Transportation Services
description: 1. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services/items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.2 in conjunction with FAR Part 13, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. 1.a. Project Title: Equipment Transportation Services 1.b. Description: VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System located at 11301 Wilshire Blvd; Los Angeles CA 90073 is seeking a contractor to motorized vehicle runs for dental and medical instruments between the VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System (VAGLAHS) West Los Angeles (WLA) Campus and selected remotely located clinical facilities 1.c. Project Location: VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System, 11301 Wilshire Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90073 1.d. Solicitation Type - Number: Request for Quotes (RFQ) - 36C26227Q0067. 1.e. Set Aside: This solicitation is issued as an SDVOSB set aside. 1.f. Applicable NAICS code: 423860 Transportation Equipment and Supplies (except Motor Vehicle) Merchant Wholesalers. 1.g. Small Business Size Standard: 175 employees 1.h. Type of Contract: Firm Fixed Price 1.i. Period of Performance: one year 1.j. Wage Determination applicable to this project: SCA WD 2015-5613 revision 34 1.k. Questions regarding the solicitation should be submitted via email no later than 2pm PST Friday, November 6th, 2026, to ositadima.ndubizu@va.gov 1.l. Company info and quote should be on the attached Enclosure 1 form. All other forms of offer will not be accepted. Your enclosure form and capabilities statement/experience should be sent in one email with 2 separate email attachments, or it will not be accepted 2. Statement of Work BACKGROUND. This requirement, driven by VA Central Office and The Joint Commission (TJC) on Patient Safety, mandates that dental and medical instruments are no longer permitted to soak in solution overnight. It is imperative that all instruments are returned to the Sterile Processing Service (SPS) for sterilization on the same day they are used. To comply with this mandate, it is necessary to arrange motorized vehicle runs between the VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System (VAGLAHS) West Los Angeles (WLA) Campus and selected remotely located clinical facilities. These transport services will be scheduled from Monday through Friday, excluding holidays. SCOPE. Contract Staffing: The vendor must provide minimum of six (6) motor vehicle operators (truck driver, class c) with valid Class C Driver s license issued by one of the fifty (50) States of the United States of America and 6 utility vans, Monday through Friday except holidays. Vehicles: The vendor is required to provide their own vehicles, which must comply with Department of Transportation (DOT) regulations, Department of Health standards, and Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Directives 1116 pertaining to the transportation of reusable medical devices (RMD). Each vehicle must be equipped with a separate partition that distinctly segregates CLEAN RMD from CONTAMINATED RMD to prevent the mixing of contaminated instruments with sterile instruments. All vehicles must be insured. Specific Tasks Motor vehicle drivers are required to perform courier runs between the VA West Los Angeles (WLA) campus and to specified remote locations for the delivery and pickup of dental and medical instruments in spill-proof containers. Each run will commence at the WLA Sterile Processing Service (SPS) located in Building 500, where the vehicles are parked. Drivers must complete a daily vehicle checklist, which includes checking fluids, brake lights, and other essential components. In the event of any issues involving the transportation of reusable medical devices (RMD), the contractor must promptly notify SPS management. Each driver is responsible for documenting the temperature and humidity levels at both the point of departure and the destination. Logs for this purpose will be provided by the SPS management team. Additionally, SPS management must be contacted immediately regarding any non-conformance related to the transportation of RMD. Drivers will proceed to the ground floor of Building 500, specifically to the rear loading dock of the Sterile Processing Service (SPS), where instrument containers are to be picked up. Upon returning from the remote destinations, the instrument containers must be delivered back to the SPS location in Building 500. Each work shift will consist of eight (8) hours per tour of duty, including a 30-minute lunch break. The remote locations are as follows: Outpatient Centers Sepulveda (SACC)/Los Angeles (LAACC) approx. 54 miles round-trip* Bakersfield Community Based Outpatient Clinic (BAK) approx. 212 miles round-trip Santa Maria Community Based Outpatient Clinic (SM) approx. 298 miles round-trip (*Two runs per day to this location; requires two drivers for this trip to eliminate overtime.) Ventura Community Based Outpatient Clinic approx. 112 miles round-trip. Antelope Valley Community Based Outpatient Clinic approx. 66 miles round-trip Cleaning: The vehicles must be cleaned by the driver daily. The driver is responsible for thoroughly cleaning the interior of the van, beginning with the section labeled "CLEAN" and concluding with the "DIRTY" section. While performing the cleaning duties, the driver must wear gloves and use the hospital-approved disinfectant, Sani-Cloth AF3 Wipes. Additionally, the driver is required to document the completion of the vehicle cleaning in the log provided by the SPS management team each day. Upon the pick-up and drop-off of Reusable Medical Devices (RMD), the temperature and humidity levels must be recorded in the log provided by the SPS management team to ensure package integrity. The temperature must not exceed 72°F and the humidity must not exceed 60%. If either the temperature or humidity are out of range, the driver must inform the end user(s) (clinic staff). The end user will then perform a risk assessment to ensure that the packaging has not been compromised. If any packaging is found to be compromised, the end user will contact the Sterile Processing Service management team and specify whether all packages need to be returned for reprocessing. The drivers will be responsible solely for delivering medical supplies (instruments) related to Reusable Medical Devices (RMD) to the various clinics indicated above. The drivers will deliver Clean RMD and pick up Dirty RMD directly to and from specific clinical areas within each facility, such as the Eye Clinic, Podiatry, Radiology, Dermatology, etc. The driver must ensure that the end user signs both the Signature and Release to SPS form and the Signature and Release from SPS form to document the transfer of RMD. Facility Tasks SAACC and LAACC Run Drivers: There are two runs scheduled for this trip with identical duties; the primary difference lies in the shift timings. The first shift runs from 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., while the second shift runs from 12:00 noon to 8:30 p.m. The departure for the first run should occur within one hour of the start of the shift. The departure for the later run is timed to arrive at the Los Angeles Ambulatory Care Center (LAACC) at approximately 3:45 p.m. to pick up instrument containers after the impacted clinics have closed. These runs require stops at both the Sepulveda Ambulatory Care Center (SAACC) and Los Angeles Ambulatory Care Center (LAACC). For SAACC, instruments need to be delivered to the clinic at the start of their operating hours, which are 8:00 a.m. Bakersfield Community Based Outpatient Clinic (BAK) run driver: The shift from 11:00 a.m. to 7:30 p.m. is designed to accommodate the later run, which is timed to reach Bakersfield (BAK) at approximately 3:45 p.m. for instrument container pickup after the impacted clinics have closed. Santa Maria Community Based Outpatient Clinic (SM) run driver: The shift from 11

title: F108--620-26-206 Asbestos Abatement
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 2, intends to issue Solicitation 36C24227R0010 for Project 620-26-206 Asbestos Abatement at Montrose VA Medical Center, 2094 Albany Post Rd, Montrose, NY 10548. This notice is for pre-solicitation purposes only and is issued to provide advance notice of the Government's intent to solicit this construction requirement. This notice is not a request for quotes, proposals, or bids, and no contract award will be made as a result of this announcement. The official solicitation is anticipated to be posted on or about November 6, 2026, on SAM.gov, at which time all solicitation documents, including the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and proposal submission instructions, will be made available. This procurement is anticipated to be issued as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Eligible SDVOSBs are encouraged to submit an offer upon release of the solicitation. All prospective offerors must be currently registered in www.sam.gov, www.dnb.com (Duns and Bradstreet) and be registered and verified as a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) in https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ at the time of offer submission and before award of this procurement. The applicable NAICS Code is 562910 with a small business size standard of $25.0 million. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $100,000 and $250,000. Scope of Work: The Montrose VA Medical Center anticipates awarding a construction contract for asbestos abatement in the Building 3 Physical Therapy/Sleep Study area. The project involves asbestos abatement within an approximately 2,300-square-foot area, including approximately 100 square feet of radiator heat shielding. Work includes the removal and proper disposal of friable and non-friable asbestos-containing materials (ACM), associated demolition, utility modifications, and site restoration as required by the contract drawings and specifications. The Contractor shall furnish all necessary labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and services to complete the work in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including VA safety and infection-control requirements and New York State asbestos-abatement regulations. Work may require evening or weekend operations to minimize disruption to facility occupants. Period of Performance: The period of performance for Abatement shall be 365 days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). All other details and information shall be contained in the solicitation which shall be posted on www.sam.gov. The response submittal address, date and time will be included in the solicitation

title: W912EE27BA002 - Lease of One Cutterhead, Hydraulic Pipeline Dredge (Not Less Than 24-Inch Diameter) Fully Operated with Attendant Plant and Personnel, and with a Draft not to Exceed 9 Feet, for Construction and Maintenance Dredging - JBJ Waterway
description: W912EE - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, Vicksburg District, intends to issue an Invitation for Bids (IFB) Solicitation Number W912EE27BA002 for the Lease of One Cutterhead, Hydraulic Pipeline Dredge (Not Less than 24-Inch Diameter), Fully Operated with Attendant Plant and Personnel, and with a Draft Not to Exceed 9 Feet, for Construction and Maintenance Dredging within the Vicksburg District � JBJ Waterway. The work consists of furnishing, delivering and operating one (1) cutterhead, hydraulic pipeline dredge (not less than 24-inch diameter), fully operated with attendant plant and personnel with a draft not to exceed 9 feet for construction and maintenance dredging within the Vicksburg District on the JBJ Waterway. The project has a completion period of 365 Calendar Days from the date of the Notice to Proceed. This IFB will be for one (1) Firm Fixed-Price Construction Contract. This procurement is advertised as Unrestricted under North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, with a size standard of $37 Million for Dredging and Other Surface Cleanup Activities. Bids will be evaluated based on lowest price submitted. The magnitude of this construction project is estimated to be between $5 Million and $10 Million. The official plans and specifications will be available on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Bidders may register on the Interested Vendor's List (IVL) at https://sam.gov/ and retrieve an IVL from the same location. Compact disc and hard copies will not be available. Telephone and fax requests for this solicitation will not be honored. Bidders are encouraged to check often for changes (AMENDMENTS) to posted solicitations. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to the above referenced website for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing. Bidders must have and maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at http://sam.gov and must include the NAICS code they are bidding under to receive a Government contract award. If the bidder is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award a bidder is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right to award to the next prospective bidder. For additional information regarding this solicitation, please contact Andrew McCaskill via email at andrew.mccaskill@usace.army.mil. Technical inquiries and questions relating to the solicitation are to be submitted via Bidder Inquiry in ProjNet at www.projnet.org when the solicitation is made available. The solicitation, including any amendments, shall establish the official opening and closing dates and times. SOLICITATION ISSUE DATE ON OR ABOUT 16 NOVEMBER 2026. BID OPENING DATE AND TIME ON OR ABOUT 16 DECEMBER 2026, 1400 CENTRAL TIME. THIS PROCUREMENT IS ADVERTISED AS UNRESTRICTED. IT IS ISSUED UNDER NAICS 237990, PSC Z1KF, FOR ONE (1) FIRM FIXED-PRICE CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT.

title: SB ERS MATOC, USACE Northwestern Division and EPA Region 2
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District is procuring a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Environmental Remediation Services (ERS) in support of United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Northwestern Division (NWD) and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 2. The MATOC will be procured on a competitive basis as a total small business (SB) set-aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 562910 Environmental Remediation Services. The scope of the SB ERS MATOC includes in-situ thermal remediation, in-situ chemical oxidation, and other chemical stabilization of contamination; operations and maintenance of remediation systems including large scale groundwater treatment plants, soil vapor extraction systems, and air sparge systems; preparation of work plans; studies with associated reports; multiple phases of field investigations; preliminary assessments; site inspections and remedial site inspections; remedial investigations; feasibility studies; Engineering Evaluation Cost Analysis; monitoring well installation and sampling; short and long term monitoring/long term operations or Long Term Response Action (LTRA); data management; data interpretation; engineering evaluation and corrective actions; optimization studies; ground-water modeling; geophysical surveys; remediation cost estimates; management of non-hazardous and hazardous investigative derived waste; environmental and human health risk assessments; risk based remediation; air emission issues including vapor intrusion; surface water discharge; applying for environmental permits; remedial design; well abandonment; meetings; public meeting participation; preparation of presentation material both written and visual; hydrological, sediment and soil studies; project reports; engineering support and/or design; value engineering studies; operations and maintenance for hazardous, toxic, and radioactive waste (HTRW) sites; energy evaluations for remediation systems; remedial action plans; remedial actions; removal action plans; removal actions; construction support; site closeout/decision documents; abandoned mines program support; and future project programming and scheduling support. The solicitation will be made available no earlier than 15 days after this presolicitation notice. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the solicitation, which the government will consider in the award decision. This notice does not constitute a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor to pay for any costs incurred as a result in replying to this notice. This notice should not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose.

description: 23 Oct 26 Amendment 08 was issued to update CLINs 0001 and all subCLINs, 0002, and 0003. Attachments 1, 3A/3B, and 4 were also updated. The conformed solication, incorporating Amendments 01 through 08, is now available. All amendments need to be signed and submitted with proposals. Due to the changes with Amendment 08, proposals due date has been changed to 16 Nov 26 at 12:00pm CDT. 07 Oct 26 Amendment 07 was issued to incorporate the attachments inadvertently left off from Amendment 06. The proposal due date remains 09 Nov 26. The conformed solicitation, incorporating Amendments 01 through 07, is now available. All amendments need to be signed and submitted with proposals. Amendment 06 was issued to correct a clerical error on the previous amenment, revised H001 and updated attachemnts 3A and 3B to the soliciation. 01 Oct 26 Amendment 05 was issued to revised paragraphs 13.5 and 13.14 of the SOW, Add Clause H005 and remove RFO clause 52.246-17 from the solicitation. Due to these changes, the proposal due date is extended to 09 Nov 26 at 12:00pm CDT. 17 Sept 26 The conformed contract, incorporating Amendments 01 through 04, is now available. 03 Sep 26 Amendment 04 was issued with minor corrections to Attachment 1 Statement of Work and Attachments 3a/3b to correct some links in the pricing matrixes. The proposal due date remains 02 Nov 26. 31 Aug 26 Amendment 03 issued with a revised Attachment 2 SRD, Attachment 3a Pricing Matrix, and removal of Clause H005. Solicitation Due date changed to 02 Nov 26 at 12:00pm CST. 24 Aug 26 Editable PDF versions of the previously released Solicitation and Amendments are available. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged and in full force and effect. Reminder, the Solicitation and Amendments must be signed and included with the proposal submission. 12 August Amendment 02 to revise documents as a result of Q&A. 28 Jul 26 Amendment 01 to revised documents as a result of Q&A. 10 Jul 26 Center Console Refresh addresses critical obsolescence issues within the KC-135 Refueling Tanker aircraft. The US Air Force needs an updated Fuel System (FS), Flight Display System (FDS), and Flight Computer due to obsolescence and is looking for innovative ideas to not only replace but improve these systems with turn-key solutions enabling supportability and future growth. The FS, FDS, Flight Computer, and the future growth/adaptability define the scope of the CCR program. The program scope also includes the addition of autothrottle systems. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Integrated Systems Network (VISN) 19 and the Network Contracting Office (NCO) 19 are performing market research to determine whether sources can provide inpatient dialysis services for its Veteran population at James Mountain Inhofe Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC), 440 S. Houston Ave, Tulsa, OK 74127. Businesses are advised that VAAR 852.219-75 VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting - Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction, may apply. Place of Performance: Contractor shall furnish services at the James Mountain Inhofe Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC), 440 S. Houston Ave, Tulsa, OK 74127. Period of Performance: The Government is contemplating a period of performance of one (1) base year with four (4) option years, which may be exercised to extend the period of performance. Qualifications: The Contractor shall furnish all key personnel and dialysis specific equipment to provide services necessary to perform onsite inpatient dialysis services to eligible beneficiaries of the Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center, James Mountain Inhofe Veterans Affairs Medical Center, 440 S Houston Ave, Tulsa, OK 74127. This will include all inpatient hemodialysis needs, both acute and/or recurrent. Services shall support the provision of Intermittent Hemodialysis (IHD) and Prolonged Intermittent Renal Replacement Therapy (PIRRT) only. Qualifications, requirements, licenses, and certifications (PWS Section 2) are stated in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). Contractor personnel shall be available at all times to include evenings, weekends, and federal holidays. title: F108--620-26-206 Asbestos Abatement
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 2, intends to issue Solicitation 36C24227R0010 for Project 620-26-206 Asbestos Abatement at Montrose VA Medical Center, 2094 Albany Post Rd, Montrose, NY 10548. This notice is for pre-solicitation purposes only and is issued to provide advance notice of the Government's intent to solicit this construction requirement. This notice is not a request for quotes, proposals, or bids, and no contract award will be made as a result of this announcement. The official solicitation is anticipated to be posted on or about November 6, 2026, on SAM.gov, at which time all solicitation documents, including the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and proposal submission instructions, will be made available. This procurement is anticipated to be issued as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Eligible SDVOSBs are encouraged to submit an offer upon release of the solicitation. All prospective offerors must be currently registered in www.sam.gov, www.dnb.com (Duns and Bradstreet) and be registered and verified as a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) in https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ at the time of offer submission and before award of this procurement. The applicable NAICS Code is 562910 with a small business size standard of $25.0 million. The Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $100,000 and $250,000. Scope of Work: The Montrose VA Medical Center anticipates awarding a construction contract for asbestos abatement in the Building 3 Physical Therapy/Sleep Study area. The project involves asbestos abatement within an approximately 2,300-square-foot area, including approximately 100 square feet of radiator heat shielding. Work includes the removal and proper disposal of friable and non-friable asbestos-containing materials (ACM), associated demolition, utility modifications, and site restoration as required by the contract drawings and specifications. The Contractor shall furnish all necessary labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and services to complete the work in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including VA safety and infection-control requirements and New York State asbestos-abatement regulations. Work may require evening or weekend operations to minimize disruption to facility occupants. Period of Performance: The period of performance for Abatement shall be 365 days from Notice to Proceed (NTP). All other details and information shall be contained in the solicitation which shall be posted on www.sam.gov. The response submittal address, date and time will be included in the solicitation

title: Industry Day Announcement Supply Chain Illumination
description: Industry Day Announcement Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Armament Directorate Supply Chain Illumination Capability Hosted by AFLCMC/EB BLUF: AFLCMC/EB requires a secure, scalable, AI-assisted federated data capability that integrates but not unnecessarily replaces existing government, Service, and contractor data sources. The capability must provide end-to-end supply-chain mapping, risk identification and assessment, near-real-time situational awareness, mitigation tracking, and evidence-based decision support for priority munition programs, initially within the Long-Range Weapons, Affordable Munition, and Adaptive Weapons portfolios, with potential expansion across the Armament Directorate portfolio. 1. Introduction The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Armament Directorate (EB), plans to conduct a virtual Industry Day to conduct market research and obtain industry feedback regarding a potential Supply Chain Illumination capability for the munitions enterprise. The Armament Directorate is pursuing an artificial intelligence-assisted, federated data capability to map critical munition supply chains to raw-material sources. The intended capability would provide enterprise-level visibility into supply-chain dependencies, bottlenecks, supplier risks, competing demands, and mitigation actions in support of senior-leader decision-making and mission outcomes. This Industry Day is intended to inform the Government�s market research under Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 10 and help identify mature, scalable commercial and non-traditional solutions that can support the Directorate�s supply-chain visibility requirements. This announcement does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), solicitation, commitment, or promise to issue a solicitation in the future. 2. Background The Armament Directorate currently lacks an integrated mechanism to assess critical supply-chain risk across its acquisition divisions, military Services, and contractor-supported weapon systems. Existing data sources are fragmented (data lives in siloed systems), contractor logistics support arrangements can limit visibility into multi-tier supply chains, and shared dependencies across military and commercial demand can create unanticipated production risk. The Government seeks to improve end-to-end visibility of materials, suppliers, production dependencies, single points of failure, foreign-source dependencies, and mitigation actions across priority munition portfolios down to the raw materials at the lowest of sub-tier suppliers. The initial proof of concept is expected to focus on PAE-prioritized programs within the Long-Range Weapons, Affordable Munition, and Adaptive Weapons portfolios, with potential expansion across the Armament Directorate weapon-system portfolio. 3. Industry Day Objectives The Government seeks industry feedback on approaches to establish a secure, scalable Supply Chain Illumination capability that can: Map supply chains from end item to raw-material origin for critical munition programs, through all tiers of subcontractors. Federate existing government, Service, and contractor data sources without unnecessarily replacing established systems. Identify and assess supply-chain risks, including bottlenecks, single points of failure, constrained materials, supplier financial and manufacturing risk, foreign influence, and competing demands. Support data-sharing standards and interfaces that protect legitimate competition sensitive information while providing the Government sufficient visibility for risk management and decision support. Enable near-real-time situational awareness through application programming interfaces and other appropriate data-exchange mechanisms. Apply AI-assisted analytics, including machine-learning and knowledge-graph approaches, to identify relationships, risks, and mitigation options across complex, multi-tier supply chains. Track mitigation actions through end-item delivery and produce evidence suitable for waiver assessments and senior-leader decision-making. Integrate with relevant enterprise architectures and platforms, including existing Air Force, Army, Navy, and digital Bill of Materials efforts, as appropriate. 4. Event Details for the Virtual Industry Day Open to All Contractors Date: 15 December 2026 Time: 0900hrs CST Location/Platform: Teams Link Classification: Unclassified Registration Deadline: 16 November 2026 The Government will provide an overview of the operational problem, desired endstate, preliminary technical considerations, and potential next steps. The agenda may also include question-and-answer sessions and opportunities for industry participants to provide oral or written feedback. 5. Registration and Participation Registration is required. Interested organizations should submit the following information no later than 16 November 2026: Company name Company address Attendee name, title, email address, and telephone number Identification of the company�s primary point of contact A brief description of the company�s relevant capability or experience Any requested accessibility or administrative support requirements Submit registration information to: AFLCMC EB, Bryant Callahan (850) 882-0260, bryant.callahan.3@us.af.mil. 6. Follow-On Engagement Following Industry Day, the Government may issue a Request for Information, schedule one-on-one market-research discussions, request white papers, or conduct other market-research activities for live demonstrated capabilities only. Participation in Industry Day is not required for participation in any future acquisition or market-research activity unless expressly stated in a future notice. 7. Individual Demonstration Sessions Although not required, contractors may request one-on-one discussions for the sole purpose of providing a live demonstration that addresses the following questions for munitions: Supply Chain Risk: Which suppliers, components, and lower-tier dependencies present the greatest risk to weapon system readiness and production schedules? Operational Performance: How do suppliers lead times, material availability, and supply chain disruptions influence production delays and repair turnaround times? Investment Prioritization: Which supply chain vulnerabilities should receive priority investment to improve production capacity, reduce delays, and strengthen operational readiness? Predictive Analytics: To what extent can historical supplier performance, component lead times, and material shortages predict future supply chain disruptions? To coordinate a one-on-one session with the Government, contract Bryant Callahan, as shown in paragraph 9. Any one-on-one session will be scheduled after the Virtual Industry Day on15 December 2026. 8. Informational Notice THIS IS AN INFORMATIVE POSTING. This announcement is issued solely for planning and market research purposes. It does not constitute RFP, solicitation, contract, or commitment by the Government to procure any supply or service. The Government is not requesting proposals currently. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting registration materials, participating in Industry Day, providing feedback, or responding to any subsequent market research request. This language follows the informative-posting framework used in the supplied Industry Day announcement. 9. Point of Contact Primary Point of Contact: Bryant Callahan AFLCMC/EB bryant.callahan.3@us.af.mil 850-797-4770 Contracting Point of Contact: Patricia Chisholm patricia.chisholm@us.af.mil 850-882-6935

title: SB ERS MATOC, USACE Northwestern Division and EPA Region 2
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District is procuring a Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Environmental Remediation Services (ERS) in support of United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Northwestern Division (NWD) and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 2. The MATOC will be procured on a competitive basis as a total small business (SB) set-aside under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 562910 Environmental Remediation Services. The scope of the SB ERS MATOC includes in-situ thermal remediation, in-situ chemical oxidation, and other chemical stabilization of contamination; operations and maintenance of remediation systems including large scale groundwater treatment plants, soil vapor extraction systems, and air sparge systems; preparation of work plans; studies with associated reports; multiple phases of field investigations; preliminary assessments; site inspections and remedial site inspections; remedial investigations; feasibility studies; Engineering Evaluation Cost Analysis; monitoring well installation and sampling; short and long term monitoring/long term operations or Long Term Response Action (LTRA); data management; data interpretation; engineering evaluation and corrective actions; optimization studies; ground-water modeling; geophysical surveys; remediation cost estimates; management of non-hazardous and hazardous investigative derived waste; environmental and human health risk assessments; risk based remediation; air emission issues including vapor intrusion; surface water discharge; applying for environmental permits; remedial design; well abandonment; meetings; public meeting participation; preparation of presentation material both written and visual; hydrological, sediment and soil studies; project reports; engineering support and/or design; value engineering studies; operations and maintenance for hazardous, toxic, and radioactive waste (HTRW) sites; energy evaluations for remediation systems; remedial action plans; remedial actions; removal action plans; removal actions; construction support; site closeout/decision documents; abandoned mines program support; and future project programming and scheduling support. The solicitation will be made available no earlier than 15 days after this presolicitation notice. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the solicitation, which the government will consider in the award decision. This notice does not constitute a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor to pay for any costs incurred as a result in replying to this notice. This notice should not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose.

PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: High Consequence Infectious Disease (HCID) Staff Training
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE High Consequence Infectious Disease Staff Training Notice ID: 36C24827Q0097 Agency: Department of Veterans Affairs Sub-tier: Veterans Health Administration Contracting Office: NCO8 Notice Type: Sources Sought Proposed Set-Aside: To Be Determined NAICS Code: 611430 Product Service Code: U009 Response Deadline: 11/16/2026, 2:00 P.M. EST Place of Performance: Orlando VA Medical Center, 13800 Veterans Way, Orlando, Florida 32827 1. Purpose This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for market research and acquisition-planning purposes. The Department of Veterans Affairs is seeking information from qualified business concerns capable of providing High Consequence Infectious Disease (HCID) training to staff of the Orlando VA Healthcare System. The information received may be used to determine the availability and capability of prospective contractors, the commercial availability of the required services, and the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether a socioeconomic set-aside is supportable. Federal market research is used to determine whether capable sources and commercial services exist. For VA acquisitions, market research also supports the determination of whether capable certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses or Veteran-Owned Small Businesses are likely to submit offers at fair and reasonable prices. 2. Disclaimer This notice is not a solicitation. It is not a Request for Proposal, Request for Quotation, Invitation for Bid, or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. Responses will not be considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Submission of information is voluntary, and the Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. The Government is not obligated to provide respondents with the results of this market research. Respondents should not submit pricing proposals unless specifically requested below. Proprietary information should be clearly marked. The Government may use information received to refine its requirements and acquisition strategy. 3. Background The Orlando VA Healthcare System Emergency Management Service supports incident response and recovery operations involving natural and human-caused emergencies. Its mission includes coordination with Federal, State, local, Tribal, and territorial organizations during significant incidents and emergencies. The contemplated requirement would strengthen staff readiness to identify, manage, and respond safely to HCIDs while maintaining appropriate infection-prevention, occupational-safety, and patient-care practices. 4. Anticipated Scope The contractor would provide instructor-led virtual training and onsite practical training. The anticipated requirement includes the following components. 4.1 Virtual Interactive Training The contractor would conduct up to six virtual interactive classes, with no more than 50 participants per class, to train as many as 300 staff members. Anticipated subject areas include: HCID definitions, examples, epidemiology, and modes of transmission; Recognition, signs and symptoms, case definitions, and clinical presentation; Standard, contact, droplet, and airborne precautions; PPE selection and general donning and doffing procedures; Hand hygiene; Environmental cleaning and disinfection; Waste management; Patient isolation and transportation within the facility; Coordination with infection-prevention and public-health organizations; Safe specimen collection, packaging, and transportation; Post-exposure decontamination, reporting, prophylaxis, and monitoring; Occupational Health responsibilities; Risk communication, patient and family education, and reporting; Support for staff and patient emotional care; and Other related HCID preparedness topics identified by the Government. 4.2 Onsite Practical Training The contractor would conduct five onsite classes providing hands-on PPE donning and doffing instruction. Each class would contain no more than 15 participants, with practical training provided to a maximum of 60 staff members. The unused slots are designed to allow some flexibility to accommodate staffing schedles. Instruction would use a checklist-based method under which participants rotate between reading the procedure and demonstrating correct donning and doffing until competency is achieved. The Government anticipates providing the training PPE, including: 3M TR-600 powered air-purifying respirators; Tyvek 800 coveralls; Inner gloves; Extended-cuff outer gloves; Knee-high shoe covers; and Hospital scrubs. The contractor would also instruct participants on PPE-waste management and applicable post-exposure procedures. 4.3 Standards Training must be based on current authoritative guidance and comply with applicable requirements, including: Current Centers for Disease Control and Prevention guidance; OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030; OSHA Personal Protective Equipment requirements, 29 CFR 1910.132; and OSHA Respiratory Protection Standard, 29 CFR 1910.134. 4.4 Schedule All courses are anticipated to be completed within 60 calendar days after contract award. Onsite training may occur outside normal business hours to accommodate staff schedules and may be scheduled over multiple consecutive days. Exact dates and times would be coordinated between the contractor and the designated VA point of contact. 5. Anticipated Contractor Responsibilities The contractor would be expected to: Provide qualified instructors with demonstrated HCID, infection-prevention, PPE, and adult-training experience. Conduct all virtual and onsite classes. Provide its own laptop and presentation equipment for onsite instruction because access to the VA computer network may not be available. Provide professionally prepared workbooks, handouts, manuals, and related instructional materials. Make virtual-training materials available electronically in PDF format. Maintain accurate attendance records. Provide completion certificates to participants. Assess each practical-training participant�s competency. Provide completed competency documentation to the participant and designated VA personnel. Administer participant feedback assessments at the end of each session. Summarize assessment results and provide the supporting feedback records to designated VA personnel. Monitor practical-training participants for signs of heat stress or other safety concerns while PPE is worn. Comply with applicable VA security, privacy, records-management, facility-access, and safety requirements. 6. Government-Furnished Support The Government anticipates: Coordinating mutually acceptable training dates and times; Providing suitable space for onsite classroom and practical instruction; Providing training PPE and related supplies; and Confirming that onsite participants are medically cleared before participating in PPE exercises. 7. Information Requested Interested organizations should submit a capability statement containing, at minimum: Business information Legal business name; Physical and mailing addresses; Website; Primary point of contact; Telephone number and email address; Unique Entity Identifier; Commercial and Government Entity code; and Current SAM.gov registration status. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

description: Request for Information: Federal Occupational Health (FOH) National Staffing Support Services I. Introductory This is a Request for Information (RFI). This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this Request for Information is to obtain knowledge and information on potential vendor interest for project planning purposes. II. Project Description A. Background: FOH provides defined health services as well as consultation to Federal customer agencies exclusively through Interagency Agreements (IAAs). FOH is a leading provider of occupational health services (OHS) within the Federal Government, delivering services to numerous federal agencies and supporting a large federal workforce. Services are provided when FOH enters into agreements that are negotiated with federal departments and federal agencies� national headquarters, and/or with their regional/local components for products ranging from a standard package of OHS program components to an array of services, including clinical services delivery, expert medical consultation tailored to a particular federal agency�s OHS needs, wellness and health promotion, behavioral health services as well as organizational development related issues. FOH maintains sole responsibility for consulting with its federal customer partners. The Vendor�s main responsibility is to provide Contractors who deliver FOH services as outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). FOH defines OHS as the seamless coordination of comprehensive services using a data-driven approach to assist agencies in achieving a culture of health and high performance. FOH comprehensive services include: Clinical Health Services (CHS) - Occupational medicine services, including urgent medical care, medical examination, employability consulting, and case review services that focus on assessing the medical ability of employees to perform their essential job duties safely, reducing lost workdays, and increasing employee productivity, as well as fitness for duty services that focus on the assessment of the ability of the employee to meet immediate job demands, increase employee productivity and improve employee performance. Environmental Health and Safety Services (EHSS) - Services to ensure a safe working environment through site assessments, environmental health oversight of all FOH occupied spaces, emergency preparedness and emergency response. Wellness and Health Promotion Services (WHPS) - Services to assist employees in achieving and maintaining good health so that they can sustain peak performance through fitness classes and wellness programs. Behavioral Health Services (BHS) � Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Work/Life and other behavioral health services designed to promote emotional well-being and a healthy life balance through stress management, financial legal counseling and professional referral. Operations and Management (O&M) � Services supporting FOH operations, management, and associated service areas. FOH services are designed to improve health outcomes and employee productivity, while reducing occupational health risks, absenteeism and overall employee health care costs. FOH�s mission is to be the occupational health provider of choice for the federal government.FOH staff plays a critical role in ensuring FOH maintains its status as the premier consultant provider of integrated OHS to federal agencies and their employees. By offering flexible, cost competitive solutions, FOH sets the standard for a culture of health and safety across the federal workforce. The Vendor is required to provide Contractor support for all occupational health services that FOH provides, including health promotion activities, data collection, and Agency/FOH initiatives requiring collaboration. Contractors are responsible for supporting FOH in the provision of occupational health services across the multiple services areas including but not limited to, account management, customer service, business operations, clinical health services, quality assurance, and case management. Contractors may also be responsible for supporting direct patient care, including providing safe, high-quality occupational health services, delivering health education, and raising awareness of key health indicators, associated risks to optimal health, and effective strategies for maintaining optimal health. FOH achieves these goals through services, including, but not limited to: a) Onsite clinical services b) Account management c) Financial analysis and cost estimation d) Billing and cost recovery e) Medical evaluations and clearances f) Quality analysis and review g) Complaint management h) Agreement management i) Specialized health services j) Consulting The quality of clinical services and strength of program effectiveness depend heavily on the expertise and experience of the Contractors. Contractors are expected to provide competent services to assist in the management of accounts and support client and organizational needs effectively. Contractors involved in providing specialized health services and medical case reviews must maintain the required credentials, licensure, and certifications appropriate to their role and per FOH�s requirements. Contractor participation in professional associations and pursuit of additional certifications and specialized training is strongly encouraged to keep current with identified best practices and medical advancements. Contractor promotion of such participation and pursuits is expected. Although required, pursuit of professional certifications, associations, and training is at the risk of Vendors. FOH will not be responsible for reimbursement. SPSs include FOH Occupational Health Centers, FOH Area Offices, and remote sites throughout the contract area. Services provided under this contract shall primarily be performed at the location identified in the Work Plan or otherwise specified by the COR (Attachment TBD). Purpose and Objectives: A. The primary purpose of this contract is to provide Contractor staffing services that do not involve direct care within Occupational Health Centers (OHCs). Direct care services within OHCs are considered secondary and are not guaranteed under this contract. To meet its mission, the scope of this contract shall cover FOH�s contract service requirements including, but not limited to, business operations, administrative, consultation, and delivery of occupational health support and direct services within the Continental United States (CONUS), and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS). If within its Congressional authority, it is imperative that FOH acts quickly and maintains sufficient flexibility to meet the need, wherever the need arises. B. The anticipated period of performance is five (5) years from award including a twelve (12) month base period with four (4) 12-month option periods. D. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: SOURCES SOUGHT: N40080-27-R-XXXX 8(a) BASEWIDE JANITORIAL SERVICES FOR MARINE CORPS BASE (MCB) QUANTICO, VIRGINIA
description: SOURCES SOUGHT: N40080-27-R-XXXX 8(a) BASEWIDE JANITORIAL SERVICES FOR MARINE CORPS BASE (MCB) QUANTICO, VIRGINIA DATE: 10/27/2026 RESPONSE DATE: 11/16/2026 PRODUCT SERVICE CODE: S201 - Housekeeping- Custodial Janitorial NAICS CODE(S): 561720 - Janitorial Services TITLE: 8(a) BASEWIDE JANITORIAL SERVICES FOR MARINE CORPS BASE (MCB) QUANTICO, VIRGINIA This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for informational, market research, and planning purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. This notice does NOT constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an announcement of an upcoming solicitation. � No contract will be awarded based on responses to this announcement. � The Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation as a result of this notice. � The Government will not pay or reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting information in response to this announcement or any follow-up requests. � There is no solicitation package or bid documents available at this time; telephone inquiries requesting solicitation packages will not be honored. All information received will be held by NAVFAC Washington / FEAD Quantico to support acquisition strategy development and internal decision-making. I Background and Purpose: NAVFAC Washington / FEAD Quantico is conducting market research to determine the availability, capability, and capacity of qualified commercial contractors to provide complete basewide janitorial and custodial services across facilities located at Marine Corps Base (MCB) Quantico, Virginia. Current Acquisition Posture � This requirement is currently performed under an existing contract awarded through the Small Business Administration (SBA) 8(a) Business Development Program expiring on March 31, 2027. In accordance with the Small Business Act and federal acquisition regulations, the Government is primarily surveying the market to identify qualified and capable SBA-certified 8(a) small business concerns (including 8(a) single-entity, tribally-owned, ANC, or NHO participants) to assess whether a follow-on sole-source award or competitive 8(a) set-aside is the appropriate acquisition strategy. Secondarily, the Government invites capabilities statements from other SBA-certified socioeconomic small business categories (HUBZone, SDVOSB/VOSB, and WOSB/EDWOSB) to assess total small business industry capacity. II Summary Scope of Work: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, management, supervision, tools, equipment, transportation, materials, supplies, and quality control necessary to deliver comprehensive custodial and janitorial services at MCB Quantico facilities. Representative tasks include, but are not limited to: � Routine Cleaning & Sanitation: Daily cleaning, sanitizing, and restocking of restrooms, locker rooms, breakrooms, and common areas. � Surface Maintenance: Emptying trash, recycling receptacles, and bulk waste disposal. � Floor Care: Sweeping, dust-mopping, damp-mopping, buffing, and periodic stripping and waxing of hard surface floors. � Carpet Care: Routine vacuuming, spot cleaning, and periodic hot-water extraction deep cleaning. � Glass & Fixture Cleaning: Interior and exterior window cleaning, partition washing, and drinking fountain sanitization. � Security & Installation Access: Strict compliance with Department of the Navy and MCB Quantico physical security policies, including Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) credentialing for all personnel. III Submission Requirements (Capability Statement): Interested, qualified small business contractors capable of self-performing the required work are invited to submit a Capabilities Statement. The submission shall not exceed two (2) pages (excluding title page) and must address the following: A. Company Information 1. Company Name, Address, and Website. 2. Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). 3. Primary and Alternate Points of Contact (Name, Title, Phone Number, and Email). 4. Location of local/branch offices within the DC-Maryland-Virginia (DMV) commuting radius. B. Socioeconomic & Business Status 5. Identification of business size under NAICS 561720 ($22.0M size standard). 6. Socioeconomic designations: Specifically declare whether the firm is an active SBA-certified 8(a) participant. If certified 8(a), state your 8(a) entrance and anticipated graduation/exit dates, as well as your assigned SBA Servicing District Office. 7. Other certifications (HUBZone, SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, EDWOSB, or Small Business). C. Capability & Performance Qualifications 8. Self-Performance Capacity: Confirmation of the firm�s ability to comply with FAR 52.219-14 (Limitations on Subcontracting), demonstrating that at least 50% of the cost of contract performance incurred for personnel will be expended on employees of the prime firm. 9. Installation Access & Clearance: Statement confirming capability to obtain DBIDS credentials and security vetting for on-site supervisory staff and cleaning personnel prior to contract commencement on April 1, 2027. 10. Staffing and Surge Capacity: Brief narrative explaining the firm�s methodology to recruit, train, and retain qualified custodial labor in the Quantico, VA area in compliance with the Service Contract Labor Standards (41 U.S.C. Chapter 67 / FAR 52.222-41). D. Relevant Past Performance 11. Provide up to three (3) relevant past performance projects completed within the last five (5) years that demonstrate experience similar in size, scope, and complexity to military basewide custodial operations: � Contract Number / Task Order Number (Note: If performed under an IDIQ or BPA, provide specific Task/Delivery Order details, not just the master contract). � Project Title, Facility Type, and Location. � Role (Prime Contractor or Subcontractor; include percentage of work self-performed). � Period of Performance (Award Date and Completion Date). � Total Contract Dollar Value and Approximate Square Footage Maintained. � Brief narrative description of the specific custodial services delivered. � Government or Commercial Point of Contact (Name, Agency/Company, Title, Phone Number, and Email). IV Submission Instructions & Contact Information � Due Date & Time: All responses must be received no later than November 16, 2026, at 2:00 PM EST. Submissions received after this deadline will not be evaluated. � Format: Submissions must be delivered via email in Adobe PDF format. � Email Subject Line: [Contractor Name] Capabilities Statement � Sources Sought N40080-27-R-XXXX � Points of Contact: Primary: Ms. Luz M. Baron, Contract Specialist Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington / FEAD Quantico Email: luz.m.baron.civ@us.navy.mil Alternate: Ms. Dotty M. Medel, Contracting Officer Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Washington / FEAD Quantico Email: dotty.m.medel.civ@us.navy.mil Questions regarding this notice must be submitted in writing via email to the primary point of contact identified above. Thank you for your interest and support of NAVFAC Washington and the Warfighter.

title: N4008527R0039 Design-Bid-Build (DBB) P-200, Aircraft Maintenance Hangar, Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THERE WILL NOT BE A SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Mid-Atlantic is seeking eligible small business firms capable of performing construction services for Design-Bid-Build (DBB) P-200, Aircraft Maintenance Hangar, Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina. This project constructs all operational and support facilities to support the basing of two F-35B Lightning II squadrons at the Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) in Cherry Point, North Carolina. New construction facilities include a low-rise, two-squadron module aircraft maintenance hangar, an aircraft parking apron, an aircraft ground/support training facility for the Center for Naval Aviation Technical Training (CNATT), a Ground Support Equipment (GSE) storage facility, an open steel-framed Operations Hazards Flammable Storage facility, and four Ready Service Magazines (RSMs). Demolition of existing facilities is required to clear the operational footprint, including the removal of Buildings 1667, 3978, 3986, 3996, 3997, 3998, 3999, and multiple hazardous waste storage shelters. The Aircraft Maintenance Hangar will be a low-rise, two-squadron module building containing high-bay space, crew and equipment space, and administrative space. The hangar will be constructed of concrete masonry units on a pile-supported reinforced concrete slab-on-grade foundation with structural steel framing, steel roof trusses, and a pre-finished insulated metal roof. Built-in equipment includes compressed air systems, personnel/freight elevators, 5-ton overhead bridge cranes, high-pressure cooling air systems, underwing and wet pipe fire suppression systems, raised access flooring, and backup generators. The Aircraft Ground/Support Training (CNATT) Facility will include administrative office spaces, five training classrooms, support spaces, and a small arms armory. The Ground Support Equipment (GSE) Storage Facility is a low-rise, high-bay single-story storage facility directly connected to the CNATT training facility. The Operations Hazards Flammable Storage Facility will be an open steel-framed structure featuring wire mesh partition separation by material type. The Ready Service Magazines (RSMs) consist of four masonry-constructed magazines (two per squadron) providing secure ammunition storage. The Aircraft Parking Apron includes new apron construction and renovation, equipped with electrical grounding, workstation kiosks, and sunshades. The project also includes extensive site preparation (clearing, excavation, grading, stormwater controls, and soil mitigation), paving and site improvements (covered aircraft wash racks, asphalt paving, sidewalks, dumpster pads, and landscaping), and comprehensive utility upgrades (electrical and communication distribution, water distribution, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, natural gas, oil-water separators, fire suppression foam containment, and industrial waste storage). All service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses (SDVOSB), veteran-owned small businesses (VOSB), certified HUB-Zone, certified 8(a), and women-owned small businesses (WOSB), and small businesses are encouraged to respond. Upon review of industry response to this Sources Sought Notice, the Government will determine whether a set-aside acquisition in lieu of full and open competition is in the Government�s best interest. The contract will include FAR clause 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (DEVIATION 2021-O0008), which states that �It will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the prime contractor�s 85 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded.� It is requested that interested small businesses submit to the Contracting Officer a capabilities package, to include the Sources Sought Contractor Information Form and Sources Sought Project Information Form, provided as attachments to this notice. The Sources Sought Project Information Form and Sources Sought Project Matrix shall be used to document a minimum of two (2) up to a maximum of five (5) relevant construction projects for the offeror that best demonstrates experience on projects that are similar in size, scope and complexity as listed below. Projects submitted for the offeror shall be completed within the past fifteen (15) years from the date of issuance of this Sources Sought. For the purposes of this evaluation, a relevant project is further defined as: Size: A final construction cost of $35,000,000 or greater. Final construction cost is defined as the total price paid by the customer for the construction services, including original contract award amount and any modifications executed during performance. Scope: New construction or building addition/expansion of an aircraft maintenance hangar. Neither pre-engineered building systems nor renovation projects will be considered relevant. Complexity: For at least one relevant project (meeting the Size and Scope as defined above), the Offeror must demonstrate a column-free open hangar bay clear span not less than 200-ft. A project is defined as a construction project performed under a single task order or contract. For multiple award and indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity type contracts, the contract as a whole shall not be submitted as a project; rather Offerors shall submit the work performed under a task order as a project. Ensure that the project description clearly identifies whether the project is new construction or repair/renovation, addresses how the project meets the scope and complexity requirements as delineated above, and provides the final construction cost. Please note that if you are responding as an 8(a) Mentor-Prot�g�, you must indicate the percentage of work to be performed by the prot�g�. A copy of the SBA letter stating that your 8(a) Mentor-Prot�g� agreement has been approved would be required with your proposal, if requested. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this project is 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small business size standard of $45,000,000. The magnitude of construction for this project is between $100,000,000 and $250,000,000. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. It is a market research tool being used to determine the availability and adequacy of potential small business sources prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of an award. Upon review of industry response to this sources sought notice, the Government will determine whether set-aside procurement in lieu of full and open competition is in the Government�s best interest.
