title: Design-Bid-Build (DBB) P-200, Aircraft Maintenance Hangar, Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina.
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THERE WILL NOT BE A SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command, Mid-Atlantic is seeking eligible small business firms capable of performing construction services for Design-Bid-Build (DBB) P-200, Aircraft Maintenance Hangar, Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina. This project constructs all operational and support facilities to support the basing of two F-35B Lightning II squadrons at the Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) in Cherry Point, North Carolina. New construction facilities include a low-rise, two-squadron module aircraft maintenance hangar, an aircraft parking apron, an aircraft ground/support training facility for the Center for Naval Aviation Technical Training (CNATT), a Ground Support Equipment (GSE) storage facility, an open steel-framed Operations Hazards Flammable Storage facility, and four Ready Service Magazines (RSMs). Demolition of existing facilities is required to clear the operational footprint, including the removal of Buildings 1667, 3978, 3986, 3996, 3997, 3998, 3999, and multiple hazardous waste storage shelters. The Aircraft Maintenance Hangar will be a low-rise, two-squadron module building containing high-bay space, crew and equipment space, and administrative space. The hangar will be constructed of concrete masonry units on a pile-supported reinforced concrete slab-on-grade foundation with structural steel framing, steel roof trusses, and a pre-finished insulated metal roof. Built-in equipment includes compressed air systems, personnel/freight elevators, 5-ton overhead bridge cranes, high-pressure cooling air systems, underwing and wet pipe fire suppression systems, raised access flooring, and backup generators. The Aircraft Ground/Support Training (CNATT) Facility will include administrative office spaces, five training classrooms, support spaces, and a small arms armory. The Ground Support Equipment (GSE) Storage Facility is a low-rise, high-bay single-story storage facility directly connected to the CNATT training facility. The Operations Hazards Flammable Storage Facility will be an open steel-framed structure featuring wire mesh partition separation by material type. The Ready Service Magazines (RSMs) consist of four masonry-constructed magazines (two per squadron) providing secure ammunition storage. The Aircraft Parking Apron includes new apron construction and renovation, equipped with electrical grounding, workstation kiosks, and sunshades. The project also includes extensive site preparation (clearing, excavation, grading, stormwater controls, and soil mitigation), paving and site improvements (covered aircraft wash racks, asphalt paving, sidewalks, dumpster pads, and landscaping), and comprehensive utility upgrades (electrical and communication distribution, water distribution, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, natural gas, oil-water separators, fire suppression foam containment, and industrial waste storage). All service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses (SDVOSB), veteran-owned small businesses (VOSB), certified HUB-Zone, certified 8(a), and women-owned small businesses (WOSB), and small businesses are encouraged to respond. Upon review of industry response to this Sources Sought Notice, the Government will determine whether a set-aside acquisition in lieu of full and open competition is in the Government�s best interest. The contract will include FAR clause 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (DEVIATION 2021-O0008), which states that �It will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the prime contractor�s 85 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded.� It is requested that interested small businesses submit to the Contracting Officer a capabilities package, to include the Sources Sought Contractor Information Form and Sources Sought Project Information Form, provided as attachments to this notice. The Sources Sought Project Information Form and Sources Sought Project Matrix shall be used to document a minimum of two (2) up to a maximum of five (5) relevant construction projects for the offeror that best demonstrates experience on projects that are similar in size, scope and complexity as listed below. Projects submitted for the offeror shall be completed within the past fifteen (15) years from the date of issuance of this Sources Sought. For the purposes of this evaluation, a relevant project is further defined as: Size: A final construction cost of $35,000,000 or greater. Final construction cost is defined as the total price paid by the customer for the construction services, including original contract award amount and any modifications executed during performance. Scope: New construction or building addition/expansion of an aircraft maintenance hangar. Neither pre-engineered building systems nor renovation projects will be considered relevant. Complexity: For at least one relevant project (meeting the Size and Scope as defined above), the Offeror must demonstrate a column-free open hangar bay clear span not less than 200-ft. A project is defined as a construction project performed under a single task order or contract. For multiple award and indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity type contracts, the contract as a whole shall not be submitted as a project; rather Offerors shall submit the work performed under a task order as a project. Ensure that the project description clearly identifies whether the project is new construction or repair/renovation, addresses how the project meets the scope and complexity requirements as delineated above, and provides the final construction cost. title: HST Roof Safety Construction Project
description: MARKET RESEARCH FOR SMALL BUSINESS FIRMS DUE BY 2:00 PM EST on November 16, 2026. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation or a request for proposal and no contract will be awarded from this notice. No solicitation or specifications are available at this time. Please monitor sam.gov as this Sources Sought Notice will not be linked to the solicitation. The General Services Administration (GSA), Acquisition Project Delivery Division, is conducting market research to determine if any SDVOSB, HUB Zone, EDWOSB or 8(a) Small Business Concern has the current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform the work described herein. All interested Small Business firms should respond. This Sources Sought Notice is being issued by the General Services Administration (GSA), Acquisition Project Delivery for Construction Services for the Department of State (DOS). The place of performance will be the Harry S. Truman (HST) Federal Building (FB), located at 2201 C Street NW, Washington, DC 20520. This is a Repair and Alteration (R&A) project�s anticipated scope of work includes field verification of existing roof and structural conditions, fabrication and installation of anchorage components, structural attachments, drilling/coring, welding where required, roof penetrations, flashing, waterproofing, protection of existing roof systems, rooftop equipment, solar infrastructure, lightning protection systems, drainage components, and occupied interior spaces, as well as testing, labeling, certification, as-built drawings, warranties, and closeout documentation. The contractor will be responsible for conducting a mandatory site visit, identifying and resolving discrepancies or constructability concerns prior to fabrication or installation, submitting required shop drawings and stamped calculations, coordinating with applicable Government stakeholders for site access, security, phasing, and operational impacts, maintaining or reinstating existing roof warranties, implementing compliant fall protection measures, and providing a phasing plan identifying roof zones, work sequence, security boundaries, access and hoisting routes, fall protection methods, and phase durations. The HST FB is fully occupied and will remain so during this construction effort. Special attention needs to be taken to ensure that this modernization does not impact the DOS�s operations and mission. Estimated Construction Cost Range is $15,000,000 and $25,000,000.00. Period of Performance is approximately 850 calendar days from date of Notice to Proceed. NAICS Code: Construction of Buildings - 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction with a size standard of $45 Million. PSC Code: Z2AA -- Repair or Alteration of Office Buildings All qualified Small Businesses are encouraged to respond. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. The main purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to assist the Contracting Officer in determining if a Set-Aside is the acceptable strategy for the procurement. It is requested that interested parties submit a brief capabilities package. The package shall address, at a minimum, the following: Examples of projects worked within the last five years of similar size, scope, complexity and duration as the work indicated. State whether your firm worked as a prime or subcontractor, contract value, brief description of how the referenced contract relates to the work described and provide an agency or owner point of contact. Company profile, to include number of employees, annual receipts, office location(s), and SAM UEI. Evidence to establish your company's standing as a SDVOSB, HUBZone, EDWOSB or 8(a) small business concern, under applicable NAICS. Describe how you will provide a fair market price given the geographical location of this project. A positive statement of your intention to submit a bid for this requirement if set aside for your socio-economic group. AGAIN, THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. Responses must contain sufficient detail for the Government to make an informed decision regarding your capabilities. Responses must be received no later than 2:00 PM, Local Time on November 16, 2026. Please submit your capability statement via e-mail to Molly A. Lewis, Contract Officer, at Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov. Questions regarding this notice may be addressed to Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov. Failure to submit all information requested will result in a contractor not being considered as an interested small business concern.

description: Description Request for Information (RFI) � Augmented Reality, Command, Control, Communicate, Coordinate (ARC4) Software and Support Services The U.S. Army Contracting Command-Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) is seeking information from industry partners regarding their experience with ARC4 software and their capability to provide ARC4 software & support services. Introduction 1. This RFI is being issued solely for information and planning purposes and is not a solicitation for services. Responses shall not contain any proprietary data from the responding company. The contracting organization responsible for this effort is Army Contracting Command � Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA). Telephone requests for additional information or to request a meeting to discuss this request will not be honored. Furthermore, those who respond to this RFI should not anticipate feedback with regards to its submission; other than acknowledgement of receipt. 2. This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. A solicitation is not available at this time; requests for a solicitation will not receive a response; unsolicited proposal responses to this request will not be considered as offers. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the United States Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, therefore the United States Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the United States Government. All responses to this RFI become the property of the Federal Government and will not be returned. 3. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude any vendor from participating in any future RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized via the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) website. It is the responsibility of vendors to monitor this website for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Experience with ARC4 Software Vendors shall describe their experience with ARC4 software. The vendor�s experience should demonstrate an in-depth and expert knowledge of the ARC4 software. Capability to Provide ARC4 Software and Support Services Vendors shall describe their capabilities to: Design, develop, integrate, test, and maintain all ARC4 software required for the integration of the ARC4 software into systems designated by the Government. Design, develop, integrate, test, and maintain all Intra-Soldier Wireless (ISW) emulator software to simulate systems. Produce, integrate, test, debug, deliver, document, and maintain any software that needs to be developed for the ARC4 software integration with Army vision systems. Produce, integrate, test, debug, deliver, document, and maintain any software that needs to be developed for the ISW Emulator to support new features, addition of new modules, updates to existing software and bug fixes. Develop ARC4 software tools and utilities as required to support integration of ARC4 software. Perform ARC4 software configuration management, to include the developing, maintaining, and updating ARC4 Software Version Documents, System/Subsystem Specifications, System/Subsystem Design Descriptions, and Software User Manuals. Develop, maintain, and update a ARC4 Software Development Kit (SDK) that enables third party vendors to integrate ARC4 more independently into their systems as well as extend the ARC4 feature set with new capabilities. Support Government designated vendors in designing, developing, and integrating the ARC4 software into their vision system and train the Government designated vendors on all software applications supporting ARC4 system operation, test, and evaluation. Assist the Government by providing technical knowledge of the ARC4 software and integration into vision systems. Provide this required support by providing subject matter experts (SMEs) with domain knowledge of ARC4 system integration, evaluation, and requirements design. Provide engineering field support services as required to support the integration of the ARC4 into the Army vision systems to include support of planning, coordination, set-up, execution, data collection and analysis. Provide software engineering and subject matter expert support in installing, integrating, operating, and evaluating ARC4 software applications. Provide support as needed for Government training using the ARC4 software in vision systems. Responses are limited to the following: a page limit of five (5) pages maximum, typed in Times New Roman, size 12 font, single spaced, one (1) inch margins. The Vendor responses to this notice shall include the following information: Vendor's name, address, business size (Large, Small, or any other small/socio-economic type), point of contact, phone number, and e-mail address. Vendor's description of their experience with ARC4 software. Vendor�s description of their capability to provide ARC4 software support services. 2. title: Authentication Services for FISMA Support
description: INTRODUCTION AND BACKGROUND This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) issued by the Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC), Acquisition Services, on behalf of the Bureau of the Fiscal Service (Fiscal Service), Identity, Credentialing & Access Management (ICAM) Division. The purpose of this notice is to obtain industry information and identify 8(a) sources that are both capable of and interested in providing commercial Engineer and Project Management Services for the execution of Authentication Services for Federal Information Security Modernization Action (FISMA) Support as described herein. This information is being sought for acquisition planning purposes only. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES Fiscal Services is seeking to identify Contractors who can provide highly skilled and technical contractual support for Information System Security Officer (ISSO) duties and audit liaison for the Authentication Services General Support System (AS GSS). Subject Matter Expert (SME) Contractor support shall include assistance in the development, maintenance, and oversight of the Authentication Services FISMA system, including Security Controls, Continuity of Operations, plans, and related exercises surrounding access to Fiscal Service IT resources. Contractor resources also support the management and response to user access issues and problems within the ICAM Division for the AS GSS system and its sub-components. The Contractor shall perform all Authentication Services; FISMA related tasks generally assigned to an Information System Security Officer and all related Identity, Credentialing, and Access Management Security audit tasks include: Provide, monitor, and manage the AS GSS as an Information System Security Officer (ISSO). This includes the creation, management, and maintenance of all FISMA lifecycle tasks, deliverables, and continuous monitoring indicator tasks within the Government, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) tool. Review, develop and maintain documentation of ICAM processes, procedures, and operations pertaining to providing and managing user access to Fiscal Service IT Resources via the AS GSS. Provide expert guidance, training, and assistance with the closure of issues discovered during Vulnerability Scanning. Perform Audit Liaison activities for the various Audits and Assessments that are conducted against Authentication Services and Central Authentication and Identity Assurance (CAIA) fronted applications. This includes the Schedule of the Federal Debt, Consolidated Financial Statement, Office of Inspector General (OIG) and Government Accountability Office (GAO) audits. Support and Maintain ICAM Organization and Identity Administration functions: ICAM Operations and Help Desk Respond to ICAM program and daily operational needs Maintain and monitor the PKI, LDAP, SSO, Splunk, Vault and CAIA service for ICAM Liaison with the AS application and service users Liaison with other FS and FRB ISSO�s and System Owners Authentication Services Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Support User Provisioning Administration, reconciliation and reporting: Create and maintain Authentication Services in-boundary and service user Policies, Standards and Procedures. Review and act upon issues seen on the Authentication Services transaction Logs via Enterprise Log Management (Splunk). Manage and review access reconciliation and recertification policies, standards and procedures for all aspects of the AS GSS. The Contractor shall participate with ongoing cloud migration initiatives, assisting with all access and security controls to ensure optimal security posture and compliance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Treasury and Fiscal Service IT Security Standards and Business Line Security Requirements (BLSRs). The Contractor shall provide training for personnel on IT related subjects centering on NIST regulatory requirements. Conduct the ICAM Technical Support (DTS) Contract Status Meeting Develop ICAM Technical Support (DTS) Contract Status Report Perform Fiscal Service Authentication Services FISMA ISSO Duties and Reporting Inventory Record of Government Furnished Property

title: FA8501-27-RAPID-990029 RPR RPL HVAC SYSTEM BLDG 300 Bay A/Headhouse
description: FA8501-27-RAPID-RPR RPL HVAC B301-OTA Under the RAPID Umbrella Framework: UHHZ990029 RAPID RPR RPL HVAC SYSTEM, BAY A & HEADHOUSE/ROOF (HEADHOUSE), BLDG 300 at Robins AFB, GA Description The Department of the Air Force, 78th Civil Engineer Group, Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, is issuing this Special Notice under the Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development (RAPID) umbrella framework and pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Government seeks industry Solution Briefs for an anticipated Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to repair, modernize, and sustain critical HVAC and associated interior building systems within Facility 300 at Robins Air Force Base, Georgia. The requirement includes replacement or modernization of end-of-life HVAC equipment; improvements necessary to provide reliable climate control and energy-efficient operations; and associated interior work to address accessibility barriers, lead-based paint, asbestos-containing flooring, degraded finishes, and workspace configuration. The supporting work is necessary to improve occupant safety, facility reliability, code compliance, and uninterrupted mission operations for Facility 300�s critical multi-tenant organizations. This Special Notice is not an invitation for bids, a request for proposals under the Federal Acquisition Regulation, nor a commitment by the Government to make an award. Any resulting instrument will be an OTA for facility construction and repair under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Purpose The purpose of this Area of Interest is to identify commercially viable, safe, resilient, and schedule-credible solutions to repair and modernize the heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) and associated interior building systems within Facility 300 at Robins Air Force Base, Georgia. The Government seeks an integrated approach that restores reliable environmental control; addresses end-of-life HVAC equipment; and supports remediation or modernization of affected interior conditions, including lead-based paint, asbestos-containing flooring, accessibility barriers, and degraded workspace configurations. The selected approach must sustain uninterrupted operations for Facility 300�s multi-tenant mission partners�including supply-chain management, network support, special operations/rotary-wing management, and C-5 cargo aircraft management�while improving energy performance, occupant safety, accessibility, maintainability, and compliance with applicable safety, energy, and Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) requirements. Solutions should provide a practical and phased path to execute the work with minimal disruption to occupied operations and with appropriate control of construction, environmental, safety, operational-continuity, and schedule risks. The Government is interested in approaches that leverage commercial practices, innovative delivery methods, and demonstrable capabilities; any use of Other Transaction Authority (OTA) remains subject to confirmation of statutory authority, appropriate use criteria, and contracting/legal review. Project Background and Existing Conditions Facility 300 (constructed in 1942) is a critical multi-tenant facility supporting several key Department of War (DoW) missions, including the 448 SCMG (Supply Chain Management Group), 78 ABW IT (Zone 4/5 network support), LCMC/WIUW (Special Operations/Rotary management), and LCMC/WLS (C-5 cargo aircraft management). Sustainable, modern facility systems are essential to maintain uninterrupted operations for these critical national security and logistics missions. The building systems are severely degraded. The HVAC units have exceeded their lifecycle, resulting in frequent failures, high maintenance costs, and inadequate climate control. Walls have peeling lead-based paint, and degraded flooring under the carpet contains asbestos. The basement east section is currently inaccessible under ADA standards. This project repairs and modernizes Building 300 workspace to prevent safety hazards (slips/falls), optimize interior space configuration, improve occupant morale, and ensure compliance with energy, safety, and UFC codes. The building 300 will remain in partial operation during the entire duration of the project. Project Areas OTA & RAPID Framework Approach This project is being executed as an Area of Interest (AOI) under the overarching RAPID (Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development) Umbrella Program Notice. In accordance with the RAPID framework, this project utilizes a Build-Only execution approach under the standalone statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Because the Government has provided a 100% completed design package and/or specific phasing and repair requirements, this project does not contain a collaborative design-builder phase. Instead, it transitions directly to rapid construction execution under an OTA structure to bypass administrative procurement lag. Competitive Selection Process Phase 1 Solution Brief Requirements The Government reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to determine that a response which does not conform to the requirements or instructions contained in this announcement is ineligible for further consideration. Interested respondents shall submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief in a clear, concise, and organized manner in accordance with this announcement. To facilitate an efficient review, responses shall be prepared in accordance with the instructions and formatting requirements contained in this announcement. Failure to comply with these requirements may increase the risk that the response will not be considered for further evaluation. The Government will evaluate them to identify the most highly qualified parties. Submission Requirement should be submitted by 3:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on or before 11 November 2026. Interested respondents shall submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief consisting of no more than five written pages (5), excluding the cover page via email to the designated point of contact listed. Jimmy Ezzell � jimmy.ezzell.1@us.af.mil Amelia Kelly - amelia.kelly@us.af.mil The Solution Brief shall include: A. Cover Page � Company name � UEI � Mailing address � Primary point of contact � Email address and telephone number � Identification of this RAPID AOI B. Executive Summary � Summary of the respondent�s qualifications and anticipated delivery capability; � Identification of any material capability, staffing, access, bonding, or teaming assumptions. C. Past Relevant Construction Experience � Minimum Requirement: The Company must demonstrate a minimum of five (5) years of experience successfully executing construction projects of comparable size, scope, and complexity. Contractors must have previous experience on large commercial buildings and or Government facilities involving Repair/Replace of HVAC systems � Focus: Historical performance in occupied facilities, managing congested site logistics, working in restricted areas (e.g., flightlines), and adhering to environmental and safety standards. D. Team Composition and Organization � Focus: Adequacy of the proposed organizational structure and the qualifications of Key Personnel (Project Manager, full-time Site Superintendent, Site Safety and Health Officer, and Quality Control Manager). E. Construction Execution and Phasing Approach � Focus: Technical understanding of the 100% Government-furnished design, methodology for physical work execution, utility outage coordination, and the realism of the proposed master schedule. The evaluation will assess the team's ability to provide continuous on-site leadership and effectively coordinate with Government personnel daily. F. Financial Capacity and Bonding � A statement of financial capacity to perform the anticipated work � Current single-project and aggregate bonding capacity, if bonds are anticipated; � Name of surety � Any other information necessary to demonstrate capacity to perform the anticipated project. title: Epinephrine Injector
description: The Defense Logistics Agency is issuing a solicitation for a national requirements contract for Epinephrine Injectors. Procurement details follow. Epinephrine 0.3 MG/0.3 ML Injection, Auto-Injector 2S in 2 count bottles. This will be an unrestricted and fully competitive acquisition. The contract will be a firm-fixed price, requirements type contract with a one-year base and four one-year options. A contract resulting from this solicitation will establish a national supply source, in accordance with FAR 52.216-21 (Requirements), to provide the items listed in the schedule for purchase by Department of Defense, Department of Veterans Affairs, Indian Health Service and Bureau of Prisons customers through the DLA and VA prime vendor programs. The annual usage estimates will be provided in the Schedule of Supplies section of the solicitation. This is a commercial item and will be solicited using FAR part 12. All sources may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the agency. A copy of the solicitation will be posted to the DLA Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil and Sam.Gov at https://sam.gov. Interested parties should contact Jeremy Brown at (445) 737-5419, (jeremy.brown@dla.mil) for any questions/comments. Interested parties are further advised to set up automated notifications of pre-solicitation or solicitation changes through this website. The current solicitation date is October of 2026.

title: Callao, Peru Infrastructure Modernization - U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) � Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA)
description: ****SOURCES SOUGHT FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY**** This announcement seeks information from industry which will be used for preliminary planning purposes. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this announcement. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. 1. AGENCY: United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA) 2. NAICS: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction 3. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: Peru 4. ACQUISITION INFORMATION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Latin America and Caribbean District (SAA), is issuing this Sources Sought announcement as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support a potential future design-build construction project at the Callao Naval Base, Lima, Peru. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. Estimated Magnitude of Construction: Between $25,000,000 and $50,000,000. Performance Period: 540 days after Notice to Proceed. Anticipated Award Date: Fiscal Year 2027 Quarter 3 Small Business Programs: In accordance with FAR 19.000(b)(1)(ii), the Procuring Contracting Officer (PCO) has elected not to apply FAR Part 19 (Small Business Programs) to this overseas procurement. Consequently, small business set-asides will not be utilized for this project in Peru. However, all responsible sources�including both U.S. concerns (large and small) and foreign entities�are encouraged to submit responses to this Sources Sought notice. 5. ANTICIPATED ACQUISITION STRATEGY: The acquisition strategy for this requirement will be determined based on the responses to this Sources Sought notice and other market research. The Government is considering several compliant acquisition pathways to ensure the successful delivery of this complex Design-Build project in Peru. All interested firms are strongly encouraged to submit a comprehensive capabilities statement, as the information received will be critical in determining the final method of procurement. The primary anticipated strategy is a Two-Phase Design-Build procurement under the authority of FAR Part 36.3. In this scenario, the Government would issue a public Phase 1 solicitation requesting offeror qualifications. Based on these qualifications, the Government would down-select the most highly qualified firms (typically no more than five) who would then be eligible to compete in Phase 2 and submit detailed technical and price proposals. However, based on the unique challenges of performing complex construction in Peru, the Government is also considering the following alternative strategies: Option 1: Limited Competition under FAR Part 6, Other Than Full and Open Competition. If market research reveals that only a very limited number of sources possess the unique combination of Design-Build expertise, mandatory Peruvian licensing (Registro Nacional de Proveedores - RNP), and demonstrated experience with specialized facilities (e.g., POL, medical, secure warehouses) in the local market, the Government may justify limiting competition. Option 2: Establishment of a Qualified Bidders List (QBL) under FAR Part 9.2. If the operational environment in Peru and the specialized nature of the requirement warrant it, the Government may decide to establish a formal Qualification Requirement. Under this authority, the Government would create a list of pre-qualified firms that demonstrate the essential standards for technical capability, financial stability, and in-country operational capacity. Future solicitations for this requirement would then be limited to firms on this established QBL. The Government�s final decision will be based on which strategy provides the best value and ensures a competitive environment among responsible and qualified contractors capable of meeting the demanding technical and logistical requirements of this project. 6. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The contemplated scope consists of complete Design-Build services�including geotechnical verification, site preparation, civil works, architectural and engineering design after award, structural construction, mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP), specialized HVAC/fire suppression, Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance coverage, and Furniture, Fixtures, & Equipment (FF&E). Facility / Scope Package Primary Function Key Technical Considerations Building 110 Spare Parts Warehouse Heavy-duty slab design, industrial racking integration, material handling flow, automated logistics staging. Building 115 Clothing & Gear Warehouse High-density pallet storage, humidity and climate control, inventory distribution bays. Building 112 Material Warehouse Bulk staging, overhead crane/hoist accommodations, heavy equipment ingress/egress ramps. Building 113 Customs Warehouse Secure bonded holding areas, host-nation customs inspection layout, physical security infrastructure. Building 114 Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) Warehouse Secondary containment, explosion-proof electrical systems, specialized foam/water fire suppression, environmental drainage controls. Building 111 Medicine & Medical Supplies Warehouse Temperature/humidity-controlled storage (cold chain capability), pharmaceutical-grade clean finishings, backup power integration. Building 120 DIRNOTEMAT & Quality Control Building Administrative offices, testing and quality inspection laboratories, specialized testing benches, IT/telecom infrastructure. Site & Ancillary Works Infrastructure & Integration Site grading, structural fill, perimeter security, access roads, utility connections, complete FF&E packages, and host-nation compliant permitting. 7. SOURCES SOUGHT: The purpose of this source sought is to gain knowledge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of contractors who have the capabilities to complete and perform contracts of this magnitude, and to address any questions, recommendations or concerns from Industry. The Government must ensure there is adequate competition among potential pool of responsible contractors. Prior Government contract work is not required for submitting a response under this Sources Sought announcement. The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. 8. RESPONSES: The Capabilities Statement for this Sources Sought is not intended to be a Request for Proposal nor Invitation for Bid, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. It is to request statements regarding the company's ability to demonstrate existing-or-developed expertise and experience in relation to the areas specified herein. Any commercial brochures or currently existing marketing material may also be submitted. This synopsis is for information and planning purposes only and is neither to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. Interested parties are requested to provide a capabilities statement addressing the following areas. Section 1: Company Information Company Name, Address, and Website Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email) CAGE Code and SAM UEI Number Business Size and Status (e.g., Small Business, Large Business) Bonding: What bonding or guarantee methods are available to your company to secure contract performance and protect downstream subcontractor/labor payments for a project located in Peru? Please specify if your company utilizes US Treasury-listed Surety Bonds, Peruvian Bank Letters of Guarantee (Carta Fianza), or Insurance-backed Guarantees (P�liza de Cauci�n). Relevant NAICS Codes Section 2: Interest and Experience in Peru Please confirm your company's interest in performing a design-build construction project of this magnitude and complexity in Lima, Peru. title: FA8501-27-RAPID-990029 RPR RPL HVAC SYSTEM BLDG 300 Bay A/Headhouse
description: FA8501-27-RAPID-RPR RPL HVAC B301-OTA Under the RAPID Umbrella Framework: UHHZ990029 RAPID RPR RPL HVAC SYSTEM, BAY A & HEADHOUSE/ROOF (HEADHOUSE), BLDG 300 at Robins AFB, GA Description The Department of the Air Force, 78th Civil Engineer Group, Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, is issuing this Special Notice under the Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development (RAPID) umbrella framework and pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The Government seeks industry Solution Briefs for an anticipated Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) to repair, modernize, and sustain critical HVAC and associated interior building systems within Facility 300 at Robins Air Force Base, Georgia. The requirement includes replacement or modernization of end-of-life HVAC equipment; improvements necessary to provide reliable climate control and energy-efficient operations; and associated interior work to address accessibility barriers, lead-based paint, asbestos-containing flooring, degraded finishes, and workspace configuration. The supporting work is necessary to improve occupant safety, facility reliability, code compliance, and uninterrupted mission operations for Facility 300�s critical multi-tenant organizations. This Special Notice is not an invitation for bids, a request for proposals under the Federal Acquisition Regulation, nor a commitment by the Government to make an award. Any resulting instrument will be an OTA for facility construction and repair under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Purpose The purpose of this Area of Interest is to identify commercially viable, safe, resilient, and schedule-credible solutions to repair and modernize the heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) and associated interior building systems within Facility 300 at Robins Air Force Base, Georgia. The Government seeks an integrated approach that restores reliable environmental control; addresses end-of-life HVAC equipment; and supports remediation or modernization of affected interior conditions, including lead-based paint, asbestos-containing flooring, accessibility barriers, and degraded workspace configurations. The selected approach must sustain uninterrupted operations for Facility 300�s multi-tenant mission partners�including supply-chain management, network support, special operations/rotary-wing management, and C-5 cargo aircraft management�while improving energy performance, occupant safety, accessibility, maintainability, and compliance with applicable safety, energy, and Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) requirements. Solutions should provide a practical and phased path to execute the work with minimal disruption to occupied operations and with appropriate control of construction, environmental, safety, operational-continuity, and schedule risks. The Government is interested in approaches that leverage commercial practices, innovative delivery methods, and demonstrable capabilities; any use of Other Transaction Authority (OTA) remains subject to confirmation of statutory authority, appropriate use criteria, and contracting/legal review. Project Background and Existing Conditions Facility 300 (constructed in 1942) is a critical multi-tenant facility supporting several key Department of War (DoW) missions, including the 448 SCMG (Supply Chain Management Group), 78 ABW IT (Zone 4/5 network support), LCMC/WIUW (Special Operations/Rotary management), and LCMC/WLS (C-5 cargo aircraft management). Sustainable, modern facility systems are essential to maintain uninterrupted operations for these critical national security and logistics missions. The building systems are severely degraded. The HVAC units have exceeded their lifecycle, resulting in frequent failures, high maintenance costs, and inadequate climate control. Walls have peeling lead-based paint, and degraded flooring under the carpet contains asbestos. The basement east section is currently inaccessible under ADA standards. This project repairs and modernizes Building 300 workspace to prevent safety hazards (slips/falls), optimize interior space configuration, improve occupant morale, and ensure compliance with energy, safety, and UFC codes. The building 300 will remain in partial operation during the entire duration of the project. Project Areas OTA & RAPID Framework Approach This project is being executed as an Area of Interest (AOI) under the overarching RAPID (Robins Agile Practices for Infrastructure Development) Umbrella Program Notice. In accordance with the RAPID framework, this project utilizes a Build-Only execution approach under the standalone statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Because the Government has provided a 100% completed design package and/or specific phasing and repair requirements, this project does not contain a collaborative design-builder phase. Instead, it transitions directly to rapid construction execution under an OTA structure to bypass administrative procurement lag. Competitive Selection Process Phase 1 Solution Brief Requirements The Government reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to determine that a response which does not conform to the requirements or instructions contained in this announcement is ineligible for further consideration. Interested respondents shall submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief in a clear, concise, and organized manner in accordance with this announcement. To facilitate an efficient review, responses shall be prepared in accordance with the instructions and formatting requirements contained in this announcement. Failure to comply with these requirements may increase the risk that the response will not be considered for further evaluation. The Government will evaluate them to identify the most highly qualified parties. Submission Requirement should be submitted by 3:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on or before 16 November 2026. Interested respondents shall submit a Phase 1 Solution Brief consisting of no more than five written pages (5), excluding the cover page via email to the designated point of contact listed. Jimmy Ezzell � jimmy.ezzell.1@us.af.mil Amelia Kelly - amelia.kelly@us.af.mil The Solution Brief shall include: A. Cover Page � Company name � UEI � Mailing address � Primary point of contact � Email address and telephone number � Identification of this RAPID AOI B. Executive Summary � Summary of the respondent�s qualifications and anticipated delivery capability; � Identification of any material capability, staffing, access, bonding, or teaming assumptions. C. Past Relevant Construction Experience � Minimum Requirement: The Company must demonstrate a minimum of five (5) years of experience successfully executing construction projects of comparable size, scope, and complexity. Contractors must have previous experience on large commercial buildings and or Government facilities involving Repair/Replace of HVAC systems � Focus: Historical performance in occupied facilities, managing congested site logistics, working in restricted areas (e.g., flightlines), and adhering to environmental and safety standards. D. Team Composition and Organization � Focus: Adequacy of the proposed organizational structure and the qualifications of Key Personnel (Project Manager, full-time Site Superintendent, Site Safety and Health Officer, and Quality Control Manager). E. Construction Execution and Phasing Approach � Focus: Technical understanding of the 100% Government-furnished design, methodology for physical work execution, utility outage coordination, and the realism of the proposed master schedule. The evaluation will assess the team's ability to provide continuous on-site leadership and effectively coordinate with Government personnel daily. F. Financial Capacity and Bonding � A statement of financial capacity to perform the anticipated work � Current single-project and aggregate bonding capacity, if bonds are anticipated; � Name of surety � Any other information necessary to demonstrate capacity to perform the anticipated project. description: U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Armaments Center (DEVCOM-AC), Munitions Engineering Technology Center (METC), Explosives Integration Branch FCDD-ACM-EW at Picatinny Arsenal, NJ, is conducting market research to determine the ability to manufacture and produce Pentolite. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT.� REQUIREMENT: Pentolite is a sensitive secondary HE very often used for NOL (Naval Ordinance Laboratory) Large and Extra-Large Scale Card Gap Tests (LSGT & ELSGT). AOP-7 and DoW specifications require that materials be qualified via these tests before being considered for use in any DoW items.. Similar, lower-grade material is manufactured by other sources for commercial mining and blasting operations. It is feasible for one of these facilities to accept a DoW contract for the higher-grade material required. Vendors must be properly registered in the Government System for Award Management database (SAM). Contractors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation of requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220, or via the Internet at www.sam.gov. This is a market survey for information only and shall not be construed as a request for a proposal or as an obligation on the part of the US Government. The US Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for information solicited. The official response must be submitted to the U.S. Army Contracting Command � Rock Island at Picatinny. title: Finland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Kuntotutkimukset
description: Helsingin kaupungin asunnot Oy (Heka) kilpailuttaa konsultit kuntotutkimuksien ja -arvioiden laadintaan. Kohteet, joihin tutkimuksia tilataan, ovat yleensä peruskorjausiässä. Kuntotutkimukset ja -arviot tilataan pääsääntöisesti erilaisten rakennusten korjaushankkeiden suunnittelun lähtötiedoiksi. Lisäksi Heka voi tilata tehtyjen tutkimusten täydennystutkimuksia. Vuosittain osa-aluekohtaiset kuntotutkimustarpeet voivat vaihdella paljon. Kuntotutkimuskokonaisuuden sisältö, laajuus ja tavoitteet määritetään kutakin yksittäistä hanketta varten erikseen. Kuntotutkimuksen tekijältä odotamme vahvaa ammattitaitoa kuntotutkimuksien ja -arvioiden laadinnasta eri aikakausien rakennuksiin, pätevyyttä tehdä tilattavia tutkimuksia ja noudattaa kyseessä olevan tutkimuksen RT- korttia tai muuta virallista ohjeistusta. Hankinta on jaettu kahteentoista osa-alueeseen. Osa-alue 1: Yleinen kuntoarvio Osa-alue 2: Salaojatutkimus Osa-alue 3: Asuinrakennuksen kuntotutkimus Osa-alue 4: Haitta-ainekartoitus Osa-alue 5: Märkätilojen kosteustutkimus Osa-alue 6: Lämmitys-, vesi- ja viemärijärjestelmän tutkimus Osa-alue 7: Ilmanvaihtojärjestelmän tutkimus Osa-alue 8: Radonmittaus Osa-alue 9: Kanava- ja hormitutkimus Osa-alue 10: Sähkö- ja tietojärjestelmätutkimus Osa-alue 11: Lämpökuvaus Osa-alue 12: Tiiviysmittaus Tavallisten vuokra-asuntojen lisäksi Hekalla on liiketiloja ja noin 50 erityisasuntokohdetta (liite erityisasuntokohteet). Lisätietoa kohteista löytyy Hekan verkkosivuilta: https://www.hekaoy.fi/kohteet/tutustu-kohteisiimme/. Hankinta toteutetaan puitejärjestelynä, jossa valitaan enintään kolme konsulttiyritystä per osa-alue. Sopimuskausi on kaksi (2) vuotta ja sopimuksen optiovuoden 1 + 1 vuotta.

title: FY27 Communications and Networking Applied Research Announcement for Office of Naval Research
description: The purpose of this announcement is to focus attention of the scientific community on (1) the area to be studied, and (2) the planned timetable for the submission of white papers and full proposals. The goal of the Communications and Networking Program within the Office of Naval Research (ONR 311) is to support the Navy's Information Warfare vision by developing measurable advances in technology that can directly enable and enhance end-to-end connectivity and quality-of-service for mission-critical information exchange among widely dispersed naval, joint, and coalition forces. The vision is to provide high throughput robust communications and networking to ensure all warfighters � from the operational command to the tactical edge � have access to information, knowledge, and decision-making necessary to perform their assigned tasks. The ONR program is interested in white papers for potential FY27 Applied Research (Budget category 6.2) projects under the following focus areas: Development of long-range VHF-band data link, using compact 4x4 Multiple-Input, Multiple-Output (MIMO) based on 5G/Commercial-Off-The Shelf (COTS) and sub-MHz frequency channelization (spectral efficiency in excess of 1 bit/Hz); Novel design and prototyping of compact electronically-steered apertures for higher frequencies (i.e., above Ka-band); Innovative approaches and technologies for low probability-of-detection communications against advanced electronic threats; Advanced techniques for distributed network control, synchronization, and/or scheduling; and New algorithms for predicting network behavior/performance or emerging operational requirements that are translated into traffic engineering policies. The ONR is receptive to innovative ideas, which are not within the above focus areas, but nonetheless are important to the Navy/Marine Corps communications and networking, as otherwise described in this Topic Description

title: Request for Information: Multi-Source PNT UE
description: Amendment 1: The purpose of this amendment is to change the response date from 16 November 2027 to 16 November 2026. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION MULTI-SOURCE PNT UE 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes (market research). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation (Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotations (RFQ)) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Due to the operational sensitivity of the Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) missions, any future acquisition resulting from this market research will require strict adherence to Department of War (DoW) and Department of Defense (DoD) security, cybersecurity, and supply chain integrity standards. Consequently, while direct responses to this RFI must remain entirely unclassified (reach out to the government contacts below for information on classified submissions), respondents are required to demonstrate their organizational posture regarding facility clearances, information safeguarding, and National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) supply chain compliance. For the purposes of this market research, the anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for manufacturing global positioning systems (GPS) and related equipment is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing) with a Small Business Size Standard of $44.0 Million, and the primary Product Service Code (PSC) for Global Positioning Systems (GPS) hardware is 5825 (Radio Navigation Equipment, Except Airborne). For specialized, airborne GPS or radar navigation, the code is typically 5826. System-level R&D and engineering services for GPS are usually categorized under codes like R425 (Engineering Services) or AC13 (R&D�Defense System: Electronics). 2.0 BACKGROUND With advances in autonomous systems and guided munitions, the force that can best synchronize its activities at a single point in time and space wields a potent strategic advantage. In the future operating environment, therefore, the Joint Force will increasingly depend on resilient, reliable, and precise position, navigation, and timing (PNT) data to execute combat operations. As such, the Space Force is required to deliver global continuous coverage with stringent civil and military position and timing requirements to assure safety and mission success. This includes at least 88% of the constellation being operationally available more than 98% of the time. Likewise, a thinking adversary will make focused and deliberate efforts to deny access to this capability, leveraging a growing suite of threats including electromagnetic weapons, cyberspace attacks, and kinetic weapons. The challenge today is that, while satellite navigation (SATNAV) through the Global Positioning System (GPS) is foundational to U.S. military operations, critical infrastructure, and global commerce, the current architecture must adapt to evolving jamming and spoofing threats. Additionally, the space and ground segments must be modernized and hardened against physical attack. To build readiness for the future operating environment, therefore, the Space Force will pursue a comprehensive navigation warfare (NAVWAR) strategy that emphasizes resilience, technology modernization, modularity, adaptability, and flexibility. Specifically, it will adopt an open hybrid approach to SATNAV architecture that weighs inputs from diverse sources according to user need, generating a more dependable capability that can withstand adversary action while enabling faster upgrade cycles to enable PNT capabilities. The NAVWAR Objective Force pursues the development and deployment of several key capabilities to advance the SATNAV architecture. One of those elements is User Segment. To make best use of diversified PNT sources, the Space Force will enable a transition to a Multi-Source PNT user equipment (UE) reference architecture that incorporates Modular Open System Architectures (MOSA) and an onboard fusion engine to integrate all available data at the user level. The key enabler of the NAVWAR Objective Force is continued Joint Force investment in Multi-Source PNT UE that utilizes both traditional and new PNT sources. This equipment is foundational to a user�s ability to devise and execute a NAVWAR PACE (i.e., Primary / Alternate / Contingency / Emergency) Plan in degraded or denied environments. While legacy signals are expected to remain supported for civil and public functions, they are increasingly less effective in the contested environment. The military-specific M-Code is available today, while the PNT modernization signals are projected to be available by 2035. 3.0 OBJECTIVE, DESIRED CAPABILITIES AND CHARACTERISTICS This Request for Information (RFI) is focused on obtaining access to analytical information on industrial capabilities in Multi-Source PNT UE the NAVWAR Objective Force. Interests include the following: Multi-Source PNT UE for Terrestrial Users on various military platforms Disadvantaged user High value military assets MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Space Service Volume Multi-Source PNT UE (various orbits) Small satellite users Large satellite users MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Interest is in technical details that can be incorporated into technical analysis to support Space Warfighting Analysis Center, Technology and Emerging Concept Assessments performed during Force Designs. This RFI is being executed in cooperation with the Space Warfighting Analysis Center (SWAC). 4.0 SECURITY, CYBERSECURITY AND SUPPLY CHAIN REQUIREMENTS The secure nature of this requirement dictates adherence to stringent Department of War (DoW) / Department of Defense (DoD) security protocols. While direct responses to this RFI must remain unclassified, respondents shall address their current capabilities and compliance regarding the following security domains: a. Facility and Personnel Security Clearances Given the operational nature of Multi-Source PNT UE and the potential for integration with multiple military architectures, e?orts will likely require access to classified information and systems. Respondents must state their current Facility Clearance Level (FCL) (e.g., None, Secret, Top Secret) and classified safeguarding capabilities. Respondents should confirm their capacity to provide appropriately cleared personnel (Personnel Security Clearances - PCL) and facility infrastructure to support secure development, testing, and operations. Please indicate your facility's current capability and experience in handling, storing, and integrating Communications Security (COMSEC) and Transmission Security (TRANSEC) materials. b. Cybersecurity and Information Safeguarding (CUI/CDI) The protection of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and Covered Defense Information (CDI) is critical to this effort. In accordance with DFARS 252.204-7012, 7019, and 7020, respondents must describe their current capability to safeguard CUI/CDI. Please indicate your current compliance status with NIST SP 800-171, confirm whether an active assessment score exists within the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS), and state your current readiness posture for the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certi

title: INDUSTRY DAY - Richmond Army Reserve Center - MILCON
description: ***THIS POST WILL BE UPDATED WITH THE PHYSICAL ADDRESS OF THE INDUSTRY DAY*** The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District is issuing this special notice to announce an Industry Day for upcoming construction requirement for Construction of a 300-member Army Reserve Center (ARC) at Defense Supply Center, Richmond, VA. The Louisville District is considering Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) under 10 USC �2808a Other Transaction Authority for this requirement. This notice is for informational and planning purposes to allow interested parties to prepare for and provide feedback prior to the official Request for Qualifications (RFQ) release. INDUSTRY DAYS USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 19 November 2026 at 0900 Eastern Time to provide an overview of the project, potential acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and potential Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) approach under an Other Transaction (OT) framework, ask questions, and provide input in advance of the official RFQ release. General questions from industry participants will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future RFQ. Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of the RFQ. Please use the information below to request Installation/Base access: Step 1: Badge Requests: To obtain pass/badge for one day or more, the contractor shall complete DBIDS pre-registration online using the following link DBIDS Pre-Enrollment or at https://dbids-global-enroll.dmdc.mil/preenrollui/#/landing-page. Once pre-registration has been complete, the visitor/contractor shall record and send the QR code/alpha-numeric code as a PDF/screenshot to the COR/PM via email (if multiple people are visiting or being vetted, the contractor shall compile all QR/alpha-numeric codes into a single email) at least 5 business days prior to visit/start date. The contractor shall include requested dates, times and names of personnel in the email. Failure to provide all the above information may lead to delays in requests being processed which could result in missed site visits, meetings etc. The COR/PM will notify the contractor upon their approval or denial. If approved, the contractor will have 30 days to pick up their visitor pass or project badge. When picking up the project badge the contractor is required to present their QR or alphanumeric code along with a valid form of ID. When filling out the QR code form, for the Service Site - select All. State � Virginia. Filter � Defense Logistics Agency Richmond. Note, a valid DOD ID card (Retired military, CAC etc.) is NOT permitted to be used to enter DCSR for commercial purposes. Step 2: Send a copy of their QR codes to Steven.Hall@DLA.MIL and he can forward them to security for vetting. Usually security will get back within a day or two of the submittal and let me know if they�ve been approved or not and then they are able to come and pick up a badge at the pass office. LOCATION/LOGISTICS Industry Day Presentation Location: Defense Supply Center Richmond � Building 70 NOTE: Onsite parking space may be limited, overflow parking is available in the vicinity. NOTE: The exact physical address will be provided in an update to this post. PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: Construction of Army Reserve Center (ARC) Location: Richmond, Virginia Agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District NAICS Code: 236220 PROJECT DESCRIPTION Primary facilities include a 56,500 SF Army Reserve Center and 1200 SF Unheated Storage Building. Facilities will be designed in accordance with the Army Reserve Design Guide. Supporting facilities include land clearing, general site improvements, lighting, walks, signage, curbs and gutters, storm drainage, paving, information systems, and utility connections. Sustainability/Energy and cybersecurity measures are included. All fixtures, furnishings, and equipment will be provided. Antiterrorism force protection and physical security measures will be incorporated into the design including minimum standoff distances from roads, parking areas and vehicle unloading areas. Access for individuals with disabilities will be provided. Facilities will be designed to a minimum life of 40 years in accordance with DoD's Unified Facilities Criteria 1-200-02 including energy efficiencies, building envelope and integrated building systems performance. The project contains options such as: Bona fide need collateral equipment. The Contract Duration is estimated at 790 calendar days from Notice to Proceed on Construction Award. ACQUISITION STRATEGY � PRE-AWARD USACE, Louisville District plans to use a streamlined competitive selection process: Step 1 � White Papers/Qualification Statements: Interested parties will submit a Statement of Qualifications (max # of pages to be defined in formal RFQ. Following evaluation of the qualification packages, the Government intends to down-select a target of three (3) highest qualified firms to proceed to Step 2. Step 2 � Pitch Presentations: Down-selected firms will participate in live pitch meetings. One company will be selected as the Construction Manager for negotiation and award of Agreement 1 for preconstruction services. The Government intends to negotiate a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) for construction of the ARC, which will be added as a bilateral modification at a later date. ACQUISITION STRATEGY � AWARD The agreement would be awarded to the most qualified Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) to provide preconstruction services and construction. Phase 1 of the CMAR agreement would include pre-construction services. The selected CMAR would act as an expert consultant to the Government, collaborating directly with USACE and the third-party Designer of Record during active design progression. The Government�s intent is to award the Phase I Agreement for Preconstruction Services prior to the 95% design review meeting. Phase 2 of the agreement would include scope for all construction activities necessary to complete the project. The agreement will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). All interested parties should monitor the official solicitation announcement, which will provide complete details and submission instructions. Draft documents may be provided at a future date for feedback and informational purposes only and are subject to change upon issuance of the formal Project RFQ. description: STATEMENT OF WORK / REQUEST FOR QUOTE A. INTRODUCTION: 1. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP), FCC Lompoc, 3901 Klein Blvd., Lompoc, CA 93436, is seeking quotes from qualified vendors for the supply and delivery of nine (9) complete fire escape door assemblies, including doors, frames, and all required hardware. The doors are for a prison facility application and must meet all relevant local, state, and federal fire and life safety codes. 2. "Equal or Better" Product Substitution: Proposals must meet or exceed the specified product quality. If an alternative product or component is offered, the vendor must submit all technical documentation, certifications, and test results for consideration. 3. Government's Right of Final Technical Acceptance: The government retains the sole and final authority to determine technical acceptance for all submitted products, based on the provided documentation and compliance with stated standards. B. SCOPE OF WORK: 1. The vendor shall provide all materials as specified below. All components must be new, U.L. Listed or labeled by a recognized testing agency acceptable to the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) and conform to the standards referenced herein. C. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS: TABLE 1: COMPONENTS: All units shall be identical unless otherwise noted. Component Requirement Quantity 9 Complete Door Assemblies Door Size 36" wide x 80" high x 2" thick Door Material Hollow Metal Door, minimum 12 Gauge galvanneal steel Core Ribbed and Insulated (mineral core for fire rating is acceptable/preferred) Fire Rating Rating must be compatible with the wall's fire resistance rating, typically 75% of the wall's rating. See required fire rating for correctional facilities on Table 2 Handing 4 Left Hand Outswing, 5 Right Hand Outswing. Frame Material Minimum 12 Gauge galvanneal steel, fire-rated and labeled Frame Type Knock-down (KD) for drywall/unit masonry or welded for masonry. Frames are to be prepared for 80 series lock, keyed 2 sides strike, surface pull on both sides and prepped for PA closer. Finish Factory primed for field painting TABLE 2: FIRE RATING: The complete door assembly (door, frame, and all hardware) shall be 90 minutes fire rated. This rating must be compatible with the fire-resistance rating of the specific wall assembly in which the door will be installed, as dictated by the building's fire safety plan and local code requirements. Category Requirement Description Applicable Standards & Agencies Listing & Labeling All components must be listed and labeled by a recognized third-party testing agency acceptable to the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ). Underwriters Laboratories (UL), Intertek (WH), Factory Mutual (FM) Testing Standard Assemblies shall be tested under positive pressure conditions. NFPA 252, ANSI/UL 10C Labeling Visibility A permanent, legible fire rating label must be affixed to both the door and the frame and remain visible after installation for inspection purposes. N/A Code Compliance Vendor must confirm that all components, when installed as an assembly, comply with relevant building and safety codes for correctional facilities (Group I-3 Occupancies, IBC). NFPA 80 (Standard for Fire Doors and Other Opening Protectives) International Building Code (IBC) TABLE 3: HARDWARE SPECIFICATIONS: All hardware must be "listed" or "labeled" for use on a fire-rated assembly, compatible with the specified fire rating, and factory-prepped for ANSI/BHMA Grade 1 standards. Item Requirement Quantity per Door Notes Hinges Heavy-duty steel ball bearing hinges, UL Listed 3 Exit Device Panic Hardware/Fire Exit Hardware (rim or mortise type) self-latching 1 set Must be a crossbar or touch bar device, operable with an applied force of 15 lbs or less. Locking Must be openable from the egress side at all times without special knowledge or tools. Keyed access from the exterior is permitted. 1 set 80 series lock, keyed 2 sides strike, surface pull on both sides and prepped for PA closer. Door Closer Heavy-duty, adjustable, surface-mounted, UL Listed 1 unit Must be self-closing and ensure positive latching. Seals Smoke and draft control gasketing/seals 1 set Required for a complete smoke-rated assembly. Threshold [Specify if required, e.g., 1/2" beveled aluminum, non-combustible] 1 unit (if required) D. CODE AND STANDARD REQUIREMENTS: 1. All supplied materials and the complete assembly must comply with the latest editions of the following codes and standards (or local equivalents as adopted by the AHJ): NFPA 80: Standard for Fire Doors and Other Opening Protectives NFPA 101: Life Safety Code International Building Code (IBC) International Fire Code (IFC) OSHA requirements for exit routes UL 10C or NFPA 252: Standard for positive pressure fire testing of door assemblies UL 1784: Standard for Air Leakage Tests of Door Assemblies (if smoke rating is required) 2. Vendors must confirm that all components, when installed as an assembly, will bear a permanent, legible label from a recognized third-party testing agency (e.g., UL, Intertek/WH, FM). E. SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: 1. Itemized pricing for doors, frames, hardware, and any included accessories. 2. Proposed lead time for manufacturing and delivery to FCC Lompoc 3. Confirmation of compliance with all referenced codes and standards. 4. Cut sheets/product data for all proposed items. F. DELIVERY OF MATERIALS: 1. Deliveries shipped directly to FCC LOMPOC can only be received between 7:30 a.m. and 2:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, excluding Federal Holidays. 2. POC: Mr. Fernando Pena, BOP Engineering Technician, FXPena@bop.gov, or 805-735-2771 3. FBOP will be responsible for receiving or signing deliveries. 4. FCC LOMPOC will provide resources for loading and unloading materials or equipment upon arrival.

title: RFI Lupus Research Program (LRP) Public
description: The Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP) seeks feedback to inform potential future Lupus Research Program (LRP) focus areas and associated research funding opportunities. Although fiscal year 2027 (FY27) funds have not been appropriated, the LRP is requesting this information to support program planning processes. The CDMRP wants to hear from all audiences, interested parties, and individuals from academia, industry, community and non-profit organizations, scientific and professional organizations, federal agencies, and the public. This RFI is for information and planning purposes only and should not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation on the part of the LRP or the Department of War. BACKGROUND: The CDMRP represents a unique partnership between the U.S. Congress, the military, and the public to fund innovative and impactful medical research in targeted program areas. The CDMRP LRP�s vision is to cure lupus through partnership of scientists, clinicians and persons affected by lupus. The LRP�s mission is to fund research to understand, prevent, and diagnose lupus and to improve treatments and quality of life of patients, including Service Members and their Families, Veterans and the general public. Appropriations for the LRP from FY17-24 and FY26 totaled $75 million. As of October 2026, FY27 funds for the LRP have not been appropriated. If appropriated, the CDMRP will utilize its two-tier review process https://cdmrp.health.mil/about/2tierRevProcess) to efficiently manage the LRP. Additional information about the LRP can be found here: https://cdmrp.health.mil/lrp/ RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: Please provide responses to this RFI by clicking on the following link: https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/FY27-LRP-RFI

title: INDUSTRY DAY - Richmond Army Reserve Center - MILCON
description: ***ADDRESS HAS BEEN UPDATED in the LOCATION/LOGISTICS SECTION*** The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District is issuing this special notice to announce an Industry Day for upcoming construction requirement for Construction of a 300-member Army Reserve Center (ARC) at Defense Supply Center, Richmond, VA. The Louisville District is considering Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) under 10 USC �2808a Other Transaction Authority for this requirement. This notice is for informational and planning purposes to allow interested parties to prepare for and provide feedback prior to the official Request for Qualifications (RFQ) release. INDUSTRY DAYS USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 19 November 2026 at 0900 Eastern Time to provide an overview of the project, potential acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and potential Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) approach under an Other Transaction (OT) framework, ask questions, and provide input in advance of the official RFQ release. General questions from industry participants will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future RFQ. Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of the RFQ. Contractors and subcontractors interested in participating are requested to submit their Name, Company Name and contact information (email and phone) to the USACE Contracting Specialist no later than 1600 on 17 November 2026. Please use the information below to request Installation/Base access: Step 1: Badge Requests: To obtain pass/badge for one day or more, the contractor shall complete DBIDS pre-registration online using the following link DBIDS Pre-Enrollment or at https://dbids-global-enroll.dmdc.mil/preenrollui/#/landing-page. Once pre-registration has been complete, the visitor/contractor shall record and send the QR code/alpha-numeric code as a PDF/screenshot to the COR/PM via email (if multiple people are visiting or being vetted, the contractor shall compile all QR/alpha-numeric codes into a single email) at least 5 business days prior to visit/start date. The contractor shall include requested dates, times and names of personnel in the email. Failure to provide all the above information may lead to delays in requests being processed which could result in missed site visits, meetings etc. The COR/PM will notify the contractor upon their approval or denial. If approved, the contractor will have 30 days to pick up their visitor pass or project badge. When picking up the project badge the contractor is required to present their QR or alphanumeric code along with a valid form of ID. When filling out the QR code form, for the Service Site - select All. State � Virginia. Filter � Defense Logistics Agency Richmond. Note, a valid DOD ID card (Retired military, CAC etc.) is NOT permitted to be used to enter DCSR for commercial purposes. Step 2: Send a copy of their QR codes to Steven.Hall@DLA.MIL and he can forward them to security for vetting. Usually security will get back within a day or two of the submittal and let me know if they�ve been approved or not and then they are able to come and pick up a badge at the pass office. LOCATION/LOGISTICS Industry Day Presentation Location: 6090 Strathmore Road (Bldg 70), North Chesterfield, VA 23237 (Red, brick building with a large chimney right past the visitors center when you enter the gate) NOTE: Onsite parking space may be limited, overflow parking is available in the vicinity. PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: Construction of Army Reserve Center (ARC) Location: Richmond, Virginia Agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District NAICS Code: 236220 PROJECT DESCRIPTION Primary facilities include a 56,500 SF Army Reserve Center and 1200 SF Unheated Storage Building. Facilities will be designed in accordance with the Army Reserve Design Guide. Supporting facilities include land clearing, general site improvements, lighting, walks, signage, curbs and gutters, storm drainage, paving, information systems, and utility connections. Sustainability/Energy and cybersecurity measures are included. All fixtures, furnishings, and equipment will be provided. Antiterrorism force protection and physical security measures will be incorporated into the design including minimum standoff distances from roads, parking areas and vehicle unloading areas. Access for individuals with disabilities will be provided. Facilities will be designed to a minimum life of 40 years in accordance with DoD's Unified Facilities Criteria 1-200-02 including energy efficiencies, building envelope and integrated building systems performance. The project contains options such as: Bona fide need collateral equipment. The Contract Duration is estimated at 790 calendar days from Notice to Proceed on Construction Award.
